Sports.title: Newcastle sign Aladji Bamba in £34m deal from Monaco to boost midfield options
Sports.content:
Newcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder completed a move from Monaco for a fee that could rise to £34m.

“I’m very happy to be here,” said Bamba. “I was very excited when I heard Newcastle were interested in signing me. I know about the history of the club and I’ve visited the stadium, which is amazing. I can’t wait to be on the pitch.”

Bamba, who has agreed a five-year contract, is Newcastle’s fourth signing this summer aged 20 or under. The France youth midfielder – who made 25 appearances for Monaco last season, impressing in Ligue 1 and the Champions League – joins the former Reims goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (20), the former Hoffenheim winger Bazoumana Touré (also 20) and the former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur (18). As a natural No 6, Bamba will be expected to compete with Lewis Miley for the midfield anchor role vacated when Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham for an initial £92.5m.

Newcastle’s transfer policy is to sign players aged 24 or under costing, broadly, between £20m and £40m and possessing high resale potential. The idea is to help ensure a club that has recently negotiated a three-year settlement agreement with Uefa after breaching European spending rules remain on the right side of football’s squad investment regulations. “Aladji adds a range of qualities to our midfield with huge potential for growth,” said Eddie Howe, Newcastle’s manager. “His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and is something we believe we can build on.”

Meanwhile, Howe hopes Bruno Guimarães will be at Newcastle to ease Bamba’s adaptation to Premier League life. The Brazil midfielder is wanted by Arsenal and appears keen to join Mikel Arteta’s team. However, the price is a stumbling block. Newcastle’s reluctance to sell their captain dictates they have let it be known through intermediaries that they will reject any offer in the region of £70m for a player who turns 29 in November.

Arsenal have still to make a formal offer and whether they are prepared to go beyond £75m remains to be seen. Much may hinge on whether Guimarães returns to Newcastle from a holiday in Brazil, as planned, next week before joining his teammates at a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.

Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool since succeeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.

Iraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his first Liverpool game on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.

“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.

“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”

One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.

“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”

Sports.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
Sports.content:
Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final.

At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history. Paredes also confronted Spain’s Gavi.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television. “But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

De la Fuente also praised the exemplary behaviour of his own players faced with these “acts of aggression” and “provocations” which he believes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Although the scenes were filmed and widely shared on social media, they have not yet resulted in any sanctions against the Argentina players. Fifa has opened an investigation into the incidents to determine whether there may have been violations of the world football governing body’s disciplinary code.

Sports.title: From Popp to Diani: 10 women’s transfers you may have missed during the men’s World Cup
Sports.content:
There were a host of big women’s football transfers which were hard to miss across June and July, despite the dominance of the men’s World Cup. Among them were Beth Mead’s move from Arsenal to Manchester City, Mary Earps and Georgia Stanway returning to the Women’s Super League with London City Lionesses and Arsenal, Sam Kerr leaving Chelsea to return to Gotham FC and, most prominently, Alexia Putellas’s game-changing switch from Barcelona to London City.

But here are 10 transfers you might have missed while attention was focused on the action in the US, Canada and Mexico.

Alexandra Popp to Borussia Dortmund

The three-time Champions League winner Alex Popp may be reaching the twilight of her playing career but her move to Borussia Dortmund, signing a three-year contract at the tier-three club, after 14 years with Wolfsburg shows she is not quite ready to hang up her boots. The 35-year-old has been prolific for club and country, scoring 112 goals in 219 games for Wolfsburg and 67 goals in 145 games for Germany prior to her international retirement in 2024. A Borussia Dortmund fan whose “heart beats for this club”, Popp couldn’t pass up the opportunity to assist the development of the women’s team, which was launched in 2020.

Kirsty Hanson to Tottenham

The 28-year-old was a top target for Spurs after a phenomenal fourth season at Aston Villa. Last year Hanson said she was working on adding more goals to her game – come the end of last season she was the third-highest top scorer in the WSL, finishing on 12 in 22 games, which was 43% of Villa’s total tally and only one goal behind second-place Alessia Russo. She heads to a focused Tottenham who are giving their manager, Martin Ho, the tools to push closer to, or even break into, the top four.

Ally Sentnor to Angel City

Sentnor, who was the first overall pick in the 2024 NWSL draft, was the subject of a blockbuster $850,000 (£635,000) trade between Kansas City Current and Angel City on 19 June. She then made her debut for her new side on 3 July, starting a 2-0 win against Orlando Pride. The USA women’s national team player has scored seven goals and provided three assists in 23 international games and, at just 22 years old, has a lot of football ahead of her.

View image in fullscreen Ally Sentnor (right) on the ball for Angel City in a 2-0 win against against Chicago Stars last weekend. Photograph: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock

Felicia Schröder to Real Madrid

Many clubs were circling but in the end Felicia Schröder completed a big-money move from Häcken to Real Madrid. Multiple Swedish outlets reported the deal for the 19-year-old forward was worth over 15m Swedish kronor (£1.15m). She attracted attention from across the world as she racked up 91 goals in 128 games for Häcken and starred in Uefa’s inaugural women’s Europa Cup competition, finishing as top scorer with eight goals, four of which came in the two-legged final against Hammarby.

Manaka Matsukubo to Chelsea

The versatile 21-year-old, who can play as a forward or attacking midfielder, joined Chelsea from North Carolina Courage for an undisclosed fee but, as one of the most exciting young talents in the women’s game, it’s unlikely she came cheap. The Japan international scored 11 goals, became the youngest NWSL player to score a hat-trick, and was named NWSL midfielder of the year in 2025. She was up to five goals in nine games in the 2026 season before Chelsea swooped earlier this month.

View image in fullscreen Manaka Matsukubo at her Chelsea unveiling. Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Johanna Rytting Kaneryd to OL Lyonnes

The 29-year-old won three league titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, including a domestic treble in . Rytting Kaneryd is one of several attacking players to leave Chelsea this summer with Sam Kerr, Guro Reiten and Catarina Macario also having departed as they revamp their front line in an effort to reclaim their WSL crown after Manchester City ended their six-year title-winning run.

Noémie Mouchon to Everton

The loss of the forward Kelly Gago, who has signed for West Ham, has been tempered a little by the arrival of the French striker Noémie Mouchon from Leicester. Mouchon did not have the easiest time at Leicester after arriving from Reims with expectations high. The 23-year-old sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury one month into her first season in the WSL and was ruled out for the remainder of the campaign. She made 16 appearances and scored two goals in the WSL last season but made only two starts. Everton will be hoping she can find the form that helped her to nine goals in 22 games for Reims in the 2023-24 season.

Denise O’Sullivan to Gotham (on loan)

The influential Republic of Ireland midfielder returns to the NWSL with Gotham after six months with Liverpool. The 32-year-old spent 10 seasons in the US before her January move to Liverpool, with Houston Dash and North Carolina Courage (albeit with a number of loan spells in Australia and England). She won the NWSL Shield in 2017 and again in 2018 and 2019 when Courage also secured the NWSL Championship, with O’Sullivan named the side’s MVP in both years. She has 22 goals in 132 games for Ireland.

View image in fullscreen Denise O’Sullivan (right) showing off her close control against Aston Villa last season. Photograph: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Bethany England to Crystal Palace

Bethany England’s Tottenham departure was mourned by fans, with the former Chelsea forward having become the team’s record goalscorer in the WSL with 32 in three-and-a-half seasons, helping them to a first FA Cup final in 2024. The 32-year-old has signed a two-year contract with Crystal Palace, who earned promotion back into the top flight with a second-place finish in WSL2. After four WSL titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, England brings a wealth of experience to Palace.

Kadidiatou Diani to London City Lionesses

The arrival of Alexia Putellas and Mary Earps has dominated the London City Lionesses transfer talk, while the acquisition of the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes for more than £500,000 has flown somewhat under the radar. The 31-year-old scored 41 goals in 93 games in three seasons for the Champions League giants following her stunning 92 goals in 168 games for Paris Saint-Germain. Michelle Kang, who owns both London City and Lyonnes, will be hoping she brings that edge up front to the ambitious WSL side. They finished sixth last season, their debut campaign in the top flight, nine points behind Tottenham, but they want more and are spending big to make progress.

Sports.title: Socceroos star Cristian Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine during roadside test
Sports.content:
Socceroos forward Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped while driving at almost 50km/h over the speed limit in Sydney.

Volpato was one of Australia’s breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup but is now back in the spotlight after allegedly driving a BMW Coupe at 109km/h in a 60km/h zone across Anzac Bridge about 1.10am on Friday.

The 22-year-old was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine. A secondary sample of oral fluid was taken for further analysis, while NSW police confirmed it will continue its inquiries.

Volpato was reportedly issued an infringement notice for speeding and has had his international driver’s licence suspended for six months, meaning he cannot drive in New South Wales. He has not been charged with a criminal offence.

Police allege that Volpato was also stopped two hours earlier on Anzac Bridge, west of Sydney’s CBD, and issued an infringement notice after allegedly driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit.

He was subjected to a roadside alcohol breath test at about 11.05pm Thursday, which returned a negative result.

Football Australia has been contacted for comment.

Volpato plays football for Italian club Sassuolo and represented Italy at at under-19 and under-20 level before switching his international allegiance to Australia on the eve of the World Cup.

He made three appearances for the Socceroos at the tournament and provided an attacking threat as the side progressed from the group stage as runners-up before being knocked out by Egypt in the last 32.

Volpato was born and raised in Sydney and played junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers before moving overseas to join Serie A club Roma.

He left Roma after two seasons to join Sassuolo where he has scored seven goals in three seasons, before making his mark with the Socceroos and shaping up as a key to the national side’s future.

Sports.title: Leeds immediately sanction exit with James Trafford set to sign
Sports.content:
Leeds United’s pursuit of James Trafford appears to be inching closer with goalkeeper Lucas Perri set for a move to Italy.

The Whites are closing in on the Manchester City shot-stopper Trafford, as reported by talkSPORT on Thursday.

3 Lucas Perri is on his way out of Elland Road after just one season Credit: Getty

Trafford, who secured a move back to the Etihad last summer, has found first-team football hard to come by since the arrival of Gianluigi Donnarumma.

And now an impending move to Leeds is set to be finalised after the club entered into negotiations with Torino for Perri.

The Serie A club have made Perri their first-choice target this summer and are confident of completing a deal for the Brazilian.

According to Fabrizio Romano, just a few details remain before the transfer can be completed.

Perri, who enjoyed a 12-month spell at Lyon prior to moving to Elland Road, is understood to be keen on a move to Italy.

Torino had originally proposed a loan deal for the 28-year-old with an option to buy; however, Leeds are understood to want around £8.5million for the star.

His exit should accelerate Trafford’s arrival at the club with the England international keen on a move to Elland Road.

Trafford had been linked with a switch to Newcastle and almost made the move to St James’ Park 12 months ago.

The Magpies’ interest resurfaced again this summer, but no offer has been tabled for the 23-year-old.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke has long admired the ex-Burnley goalkeeper, who is set to become the club’s first-choice between the posts next season.

3 James Trafford is edging closer to a permanent move to Leeds Credit: Getty

3 Leeds boss Daniel Farke is a long-term admirer of Trafford Credit: AFP

A busy window

Farke has been active so far in the summer transfer window, having added two fresh faces to his squad.

Leeds have wrapped up the signing of Bosnian centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, and he joins free-agent signing Harry Wilson after his departure from Fulham.

Farke led Leeds to a 15th-place finish last season, steering his side away from a relegation dogfight.

The Whites finished nine points above the bottom three thanks to a good run of late-season form.

Leeds kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign at Nottingham Forest on Saturday, August 22.

Fixtures against Brentford, Brighton and Newcastle follow for Farke's side, who will be confident of getting early-season points on the board.

Sports.title: New Belgium boss Mark van Bommel recruits ex-Premier League star as assistant
Sports.content:
Mark van Bommel has been appointed as Belgium's new manager on a two-year deal.

The former Netherlands midfielder replaces Rudi Garcia in the dugout, with his contract running until the end of Euro 2028.

3 Van Bommel has been appointed Belgium manager on a two-year deal Credit: Getty

Garcia departed as manager following a quarter-final defeat to Spain at the World Cup.

The Belgian FA subsequently confirmed that his contract would not be extended beyond the tournament.

Van Bommel has now been confirmed as his replacement and will lead the national team in the Nations League as well as Euro 2028 qualifying.

His first match in charge against Italy is scheduled for September 25 before fixtures against both France and Turkey during the league phase.

The 49-year-old had been available after leaving Belgian side Royal Antwerp in 2024.

His two years in charge saw Van Bommel win a league and cup double as well as the Belgian Super Cup.

It followed previous spells with both PSV and Wolfsburg, whilst he has also served as both Saudi Arabia and Australia assistant manager in the past.

As a player, Van Bommel won 79 caps for the Netherlands and was part of the side which reached the 2010 World Cup final.

Coaching staff revealed

Having confirmed his appointment, Van Bommel's Belgium backroom staff has also been revealed.

Amongst them is former Premier League star Boudewijn Zenden.

3 Former Premier League winger Zenden has been named as part of Van Bommel's backroom staff Credit: Alamy

The ex-Netherlands international is a familiar face to fans of Chelsea, Liverpool and Sunderland.

Zenden also played for PSV, Barcelona and Sunderland during his career.

Since retiring in 2011, the 49-year-old has held several coaching roles, most recently with Dutch second-tier side MVV Maastricht.

Meanwhile, he previously served as a coach under Van Bommel at PSV as well as being a team-mate of his at youth and senior international level.

The new manager's coaching team also includes former Belgium midfielder Maarten Martens and Dutch coach Reinier Robbemond.

Van Bommel statement

Following his appointment, Van Bommel explained: "It is a great honour to become head coach of Belgium. I would like to thank the Royal Belgian Football Association for their confidence in me.

3 Van Bommel has been tasked with overseeing Belgium's Nations League and Euro 2028 qualifying campaigns Credit: AFP

"Belgium has outstanding players and enormous potential. Together with my coaching staff, we want to build a team that is disciplined, ambitious and brave enough to compete with the very best.

"Success is never guaranteed, but hard work, honesty and commitment are.

"We will give everything to help this team improve every day and make the Belgian people proud.

"I am looking forward to meeting the players, the staff and the supporters, and beginning this new chapter together."

Van Bommel's first task as manager will be to qualify for the Nations League finals for the first time since 2021.

His side will then be aiming to reach a fourth successive European Championship in two years' time.

Sports.title: Defiant Argentina president claims ‘people are jealous’ as he claps back at criticism of World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
FIFA is investigating Argentina over antics in the World Cup final, but President Milei believes the backlash over his nation's campaign comes down to jealously

Defiant Argentina president claims ‘people are jealous’ as he claps back at criticism of World Cup campaign

Argentina's president has declared people are 'jealous' of his nation amid criticism over the team's World Cup antics.

Javier Milei has been outspoken following La Albiceleste's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the final, and was embarrassed on Monday after he appeared to accidentally publish a scheduled X post celebrating victory.



4 Argentina's president believes many are 'jealous' of the World Cup runners up Credit: Getty

He also bizarrely announced a national holiday that the public might not get, much to the delight of many fans who believed Argentina didn't deserve to win the 2026 tournament based on their negative performances throughout.

A turbulent summer, which featured a row over the Falkland Islands following a semi-final win over England, was capped when Leandro Paredes sparked a brawl by appearing to throw a punch at the final whistle in the World Cup final.

Other players have been described as 'classless' for turning their backs on Spain's celebrations.



Milei, though, believes much of the backlash comes down to jealousy.

"The problem with Argentina is that we are flashy, we don't go unnoticed, people are jealous of us, and we are good at almost everything," the libertarian leader said.

"I'm sorry, but someone had to say it."

Milei watched the final from his home, instead of MetLife Stadium, out of superstition. Argentina still lost the match.



Speaking specifically of the defeat against Spain in an interview with La Nacion, he added: "The match was extremely difficult for us on Sunday, and yet Argentina could have grabbed an equaliser in the final minutes.

"Even though the run of play was not at all favourable, Argentina always took up stances and behaved in a measured manner throughout the tournament.



"Even in the moments when the referee took incorrect positions towards the Argentina national team in some matches, they responded in a very measured and organised way, and they were always distinguished fighting until the end."

4 Milei has praised Argentina for 'distinguished fighting' in the World Cup final Credit: AFP

4 FIFA is investigating the team over their conduct at full-time Credit: Getty

Contrary to Milei's suggestion of a 'distinguished' effort, FIFA has confirmed Argentina are under investigation for their conduct in the World Cup final, and a fan petition calling for the team to be banned for life was recently signed by 23 million people.



Spain head coach says Argentina behaviour 'intolerable and unacceptable'

Meanwhile, Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has broken his silence on Argentina's conduct after the final whistle on Sunday, and described it as 'intolerable and unacceptable.'

"At the time, I didn't realise it. I was celebrating, hugging team-mates," he told Spanish television.

"But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed.

"Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.



"I want to highlight our behaviour in the face of that kind of aggression and provocation. Our players always kept their composure and behaved like true professionals."

4 De La Fuente has branded Argentina's conduct 'intolerable and unacceptable' Credit: Getty

FIFA has said post-match incidents, which included a Paredes being shown a red card for violent conduct, and Nahuel Molina attempting to knock over Spain midfielder Rodri as he celebrated, are being investigated.

"The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has appointed a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents," a statement read.



"Further details will be communicated by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee once the prosecutor's report has been completed."

Sports.title: Spain manager lashes out at ‘intolerable and unacceptable’ Argentina in furious statement after World Cup
Sports.content:
Spain manager lashes out at ‘intolerable and unacceptable’ Argentina in furious statement after World Cup

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has slammed the behaviour of Argentina players in the moments after his side’s World Cup triumph.

Various tussles took place on the pitch at MetLife Stadium after the final whistle, marring Spain’s 1-0 victory over Lionel Scaloni’s side.



5 Leandro Paredes aggressively hit out at Gavi after the final whistle Credit: Getty

5 But Spain had the last laugh by claiming their second World Cup success Credit: AFP

Argentina stars Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes were seen to be in the thick of the melee as they targeted Spain duo Rodri and Eric Garcia.

The South Americans did not take kindly to the defeat nor Spain’s celebration in the aftermath with Paredes also seen squabbling with Spanish midfield ace Gavi.



What did De La Fuente say about the incidents?

Speaking for the first time about the post-match incidents, De La Fuente hit out at the conduct of Argentina’s stars.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television.



“But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed.

"Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”



The Spain boss paid tribute to the behaviour of his players who kept their cool in the face of intense ‘aggression’ and ‘provocation’.

De La Fuente believes the skirmishes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Argentina are yet to face any disciplinary action despite various angles of the scenes being shared across social media platforms.

FIFA has opened an investigation into the incidents to assess whether Argentina had breached their disciplinary code.



5 Argentina players allowed their frustrations to boil over at full-time Credit: Getty

5 Luis De la Fuente hit out at the conduct of Argentina's stars Credit: Getty

It comes after a petition was launched to inflict a lifetime World Cup ban on Argentina.

In under a week, the petition has garnered a whopping 23 million signatures from 170 countries across the globe.



Fans had become fed up with the South Americans’ antics while accusing FIFA and match referees of 'bias' towards Argentina and captain Lionel Messi.

A new era approaching

Argentina are set for a huge shake up in the wake of last weekend’s World Cup final defeat.

Messi has been tipped to announce his retirement from international football at the age of 39.

Goalkeeper Emi Martinez hinted that he could soon follow suit having played a key role in the past two World Cup campaigns.



5 There will be plenty for Messi to ponder in the coming days and weeks Credit: Getty

Veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi went one better by already announcing his international retirement.

Argentina boss Scaloni’s future is also uncertain after telling reporters that he could call it quits when his contract expires at the end of 2026.

Sports.title: US soccer fans joke we’re a ‘proper football country now’ after booing World Cup villain on MLS return
Sports.content:
Matt Freese's World Cup nightmare isn't over as the New York City FC goalkeeper was brutally singled out on the road.

U.S. soccer culture may be learning from Europe and South America.

USMNT goalkeeper Matt Freese had a rough game in the defeat to Belgium, making a mess of things after rushing out of his box and allowing the Red Devils to go 3-1 up.

3 Crew fans let Freese have it after his mistake for USMNT in the World Cup Credit: Getty



In days gone by, Major League Soccer has been accused of being a bit of a soft touch compared to the top leagues in countries where The Beautiful Game is the national sport.

Freese may be wishing that was still the case having been booed in a road game for New York City.

Columbus Crew fans jeered him every time he touched the ball, apparently still angry about his perceived role in the USMNT's elimination.

In truth, Freese is an easy scapegoat but the team was outplayed by a Belgium side still furious that Folarin Balogun had been allowed to play.



On the bright side, fans believe that this latest development might be the start of a true soccer culture developing.

"We are finally becoming a proper footballing country," joked one.

"And still miles above Turner. May this heckle continue for him to grow," added another.



"Nah, in London they would sing a song for six minutes about how much he sucks," a third wrote.

Freese's City had the last laugh, however, with a 2-1 victory.

After the game, manager Pascal Jansen praised his No. 1.

3 Freese was gutted after his blunder Credit: Getty



"It was almost the whole stadium that booing him, trying to get him off his game," he said. "But if you look back at how he handled himself, you can only give him a massive compliment for how he presented himself."

The keeper will get a run of home games next with New York hosting the Chicago Fire and Toronto FC at Etihad Park in MLS on July 25 and 31, and Santos Laguna in the Leagues Cup on August 6.

Inter Miami's Rocco Ríos Novo slammed on social media

There are plenty of new fans tuning in after the World Cup on home soil.

Unfortunately for Inter Miami No. 1 Rocco Ríos Novo, he had a nightmare of his own in a 3-2 win over Chicago Fire.



Miami defender Ian Fray rolled the ball to his goalkeeper in the 18th minute and he took a wild swing with his right boot, missed completely and saw the ball trickle into his own goal.

Fans questioned the quality of MLS on social media.

3 The USMNT No. 1 will have to pick himself back up Credit: Getty

"I decided to give the MLS a shot after watching the entire World Cup. Then this happened," wrote one.

He later added: "I’m sure this is an outlier but man the quality is so far down from the World Cup it’s crazy."



"MLS delivering peak comedy as usual. That keeper looked traumatised," added another.

"Messi wasn’t crying because he lost the World Cup he was crying because he knew he had to go back to this," read one brutal joke.

"You must have forgot what the US goalie did against Belgium then," another chimed in reference to Freese.

Sports.title: ‘Idiots’ who filmed England Youth scrap slammed as questions raised over how it was leaked
Sports.content:
‘Idiots’ who filmed England Youth scrap slammed as questions raised over how it was leaked

Footage of England Youth players fighting in a hotel room has been labelled a 'nothing burger' by Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony.

It comes after a video from late 2025 surfaced on social media this week.

3 The FA says footage of under-16 players fighting was caused by an 'internal matter' and was 'quickly resolved' Credit: Getty

The viral clip shows two members of the Three Lions' under-16 side fighting at a camp in Sedi, Turkey.

An under-16s side played matches against Turkey, Wales and Portugal during the trip in October and November last year.

Youth team incident

During the confrontation, their team-mates can be seen filming and encouraging them, the videos shows.

According to the FA, the incident was caused by an 'internal matter' which was 'quickly resolved'.

In the minute-long video, a boy wearing official England kit can be seen grabbing a mobile phone from a team-mate laid on the bed of a hotel room.

The following scuffle over the device leads to punches, kicks and grappling.

Footage of the incident also shows the boy who attempted to snatch the phone putting the other boy in a headlock.

He then drags him around the room before throwing him onto the floor.

In a statement, an FA spokesperson said: "We were made aware of an internal matter during an Under-16s camp in October 2025. This was quickly resolved at the time."

talkSPORT verdict

Peterborough chairman MacAnthony has now shared his stance on the video.

3 MacAnthony has dismissed the relevance of the fight involving England youth team players Credit: Talksport

The Posh co-owner discussed the incident alongside Alex Crook live on talkSPORT on Friday morning.

Giving his reaction, he admitted: "I make nothing of it. It was dealt with by the FA a few years ago. It was a load of 16-year-olds having a scuffle.

"It goes on every day, everywhere in the world. I guess they’re held to a higher standard because they’re young footballers.

"I’ve got two problems with it, not with the two idiots who were fighting. I’ve got a problem with the idiot stood there filming it.

"I think that’s modern day for you. That everyone’s behind a camera phone and nobody intervened. Back in the day, I would have stepped in and gone, ‘what are you doing? You pair of morons.’

"And I’ve got an issue with whoever leaked it, and again, that’s the world we live in nowadays. That shouldn’t even be out in the press. I don’t know why the media are even talking about it."

3 The incident occurred during an England under-16 camp in Turkey in late 2025 Credit: Getty

Referring to the fallout from the footage emerging, MacAnthony added: "It goes on up and down the country. Every football club, by the way and I’ll give you an example.

"Our academy, years ago, and these players are gone. One of them we sold for a lot of money.

"We had two players who were caught shoplifting when they were 14. They were in our academy.

"And one of them, when they got caught, nearly arrested and the police came, he gave another academy player’s name and dobbed him in instead. Now, is that national news? Is that important?"

Boys will be boys?

When asked by Crook if the incident is a case of 'boys being boys', MacAnthony dismissed the suggestion, though.

He instead explained: "No, I’m not saying it’s boys being boys because you don’t want to see any of that crap go on. What I’m saying is we’re blowing it up.

"It’s a nothing burger that, again, the media are outraged about. They’re two idiots obviously rowing, it doesn’t matter if they’re in an England kit.

"They’re both under 16 and, honestly, you call that a fight? It’s fisticuffs, is basically what it is.

"Like I said, my issue is with the idiots watching and whoever leaked it from a camera phone.

"That’s obviously somebody who’s probably not in football anymore, has been released, who thought I’m going to put that out."

Sports.title: Man United transfer news: Red Devils to sign another premium midfielder from extensive list of targets
Sports.content:
Man United transfer news: Red Devils to sign another premium midfielder from extensive list of targets

France star Manu Kone is just one name on Manchester United's list of premium midfield targets.

The Red Devils have made the centre of the park a priority position this summer, already snapping up Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from Premier League rivals Aston Villa and Chelsea.



5 Manu Kone and Aurelien Tchouameni are both on Man United's radar, having been teammates all summer with France Credit: Getty

Their transfer activity comes as Michael Carrick looks to bolster his squad ahead of the club's return to the Champions League in the upcoming season.

And United could continue their business by turning their attention to two midfielders from France's recent World Cup campaign.

According to talkSPORT's Chief Transfer Correspondent Alex Crook, they are keen on both Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni and Roma's Kone.



With the Spanish giants looking to snap up Manchester City's World Cup-winning captain Rodri, newly-appointed boss Jose Mourinho is reportedly open to selling Tchouameni to free up funds for this.

talkSPORT understands Rodri is pushing for a move to the Santiago Bernabeu, who has just a year left on his City contract.



But while United striking up a deal for Tchouamni would help Real here, he isn't the only Frenchman on their wish list.

talkSPORT previously reported that the Red Devils had made an enquiry about Kone, who impressed in the heart of France's midfield at the World Cup and is expected to leave Roma this summer.



Take Tchou?

With reports linking United with both Tchouameni, as well as his Real Madrid teammate Eduardo Camavinga, talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent revealed on Friday's Breakfast that Kone is another of the club's midfield targets.

Crook said: "Kone as well [is a target].

"They've got an extensive list. I am confident they will sign one more midfielder between now and the end of the window.

5 Michael Carrick is currently overseeing his first transfer window as Man United boss Credit: Getty

5 Fresh from winning the World Cup, Rodri is key to any deal involving Tchouameni at United Credit: Getty



"For now, they are just keeping their powder dry and hoping some prices come down because it's a long time until the Premier League season starts.

"What Manchester United don't want to do is commit the mistakes of previous years and end up overpaying.

"I think the two they've got in for £85million combined - Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans - is a good start."

United have focused on bolstering their midfield this summer after the departure of veteran star Casemiro, who has joined Inter Miami.



Manuel Ugarte was also expected to be sold, but he is now facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Uruguay, meaning the Red Devils need to rebuild in the position either way.

The signing of either Kone or Tchouameni would certainly bring plenty of pedigree, with both having showcased their ability at the highest level.

5 Manu Kone's ball-carrying abilities are admired by United boss Michael Carrick Credit: Getty

Kone started in four of his five World Cup appearances for France this summer, as they reached the semi-finals.



Having joined Roma last summer, he also shone in his debut season, playing 29 Serie A games to help his side to Champions League qualification.

Meanwhile Tchouameni was in the starting XI in Les Bleus' 2022 World Cup final defeat to Argentina, and boasts the 2024 Champions League among his silverware with Real Madrid.

Crook: Man United not done yet

While Crook praised United for their shrewd business so far, he admitted there are still areas where they must strengthen.

He continued: "They do need another midfielder. They probably need another left-back as well."



“[Newcastle full-back] Lewis Hall is on their radar, because Luke Shaw is not going to play every minute of every game, certainly not when you're factoring the Champions League as well.

5 Michael Carrick is currently overseeing his first transfer window as Man United boss Credit: Getty

"And I think they probably need another forward, because in an ideal world, you'd move on Joshua Zirkzee and bring in someone a bit more prolific. “

Sports.title: Two new Chelsea signings already injured and left at home for pre-season tour
Sports.content:
Two new Chelsea signings already injured and left at home for pre-season tour

Emmanuel Emegha will miss the first leg of Chelsea's tour to Australia having picked up an injury in a friendly, talkSPORT understands.

Emegha sustained a hamstring issue during the Blues' 3-0 win over League One side Bromley, which was played behind closed doors.



2 Emegha's Chelsea career has got off to a tricky start Credit: AFP

The Dutch international was subsequently not included in the Chelsea squad bound for pre-season games in Australia and Asia.

Another notable absentee from the travelling party was Geovany Quneda, who has a minor fitness issue.

It's a cruel start to life for the duo, who both officially joined Chelsea this summer.



Emegha arrived from the Blues' sister club Strasbourg on the back of a season where he scored eight goals in 18 matches across all competitions.

However, the 23-year-old struggled with his fitness in the 2025/26 campaign as he missed a total of 33 matches for Strasbourg with injury.



Chelsea beat Manchester United to Quenda in March last year, although the transfer would not take place until this summer.

The 19-year-old arrived at Stamford Bridge on an eight-year deal, with the Blues understood to have paid an estimated £42m to prise him away from Sporting.



Emegha and Quenda's respective additions continue what has been a hectic summer for the Blues.

Chelsea unafraid to splash the cash

Overseen by new manager Xabi Alonso, who was appointed in May, Chelsea have already spent upwards of £200m.

The headline act of the west London outfit's summer spending to date is Morgan Rogers, who joined from Aston Villa for an eye-watering £117m.

2 Despite signing for the Blues, Rogers won't be on their pre-season trip as he gets an extended break after the World Cup Credit: Getty



Chelsea's travelling squad for pre-season Goalkeepers: Filip Jorgensen, Robert Sanchez, Ted Curd, Teddy Sharman-Lowe Defenders: Josh Acheampong, Tosin Adarabioyo, Aaron Anselmino, Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Jorrel Hato, Marco Palestra, Mamadou Sarr, Tayo Subuloye Midfielders: Landon Emenalo, Dario Essugo, Omari Kellyman, Romeo Lavia, Madhi Nicoll-Jazuli, Reggie Walsh, Reggie Watson Forwards: Liam Delap, Jamie Gittens, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, Dastan Satpeyev, Estevao Willian

Rogers' transfer fee made him the most expensive British player of all time.

Chelsea were also convinced to part with £47m for Italy international Marco Palestra.

Palestra initially seemed destined to join Inter Milan from Atalanta, but Chelsea pipped the Serie A champions to the post.

Chelsea's expenditure to date has been aided by a string of major outgoings.



Midfielder Andrey Santos made the switch to Manchester United for £50m while Marc Cucurella, who helped Spain win the World Cup, joined Real Madrid for an initial £47.5m.

The Blues also have got winger Alejandro Garnacho off their books as Aston Villa recruited him on a season-long loan with a conditional obligation to buy.

Sports.title: LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers as NBA icon finally makes a decision on his future
Sports.content:
LeBron James has stunned the NBA by signing with the Philadelphia 76ers.

It ends the uncertainty over the NBA icon's future that has dominated the offseason and brings his spell with the Los Angeles Lakers to an end after an eight-season run highlighted by the 2020 NBA title.

James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey as he pursues an elusive fifth NBA title.

He is set to sign a modest $8-million, two-year contract with the Sixers, according to ESPN. He made nearly $53 million last season.

In a lengthy statement on X, the 41-year-old admitted he strongly considered retiring but believes he still has 'more to give' and can turn his new team into a contender.

He wrote: 'I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game.

LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal

The 41-year-old, pictured with wife Savannah, has spent the summer deciding his future

James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown

'I still truly love this game, and I have more to give. The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out.

'This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship.

'I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!'

James told the Lakers earlier this summer that he would not be returning to Los Angeles next season.

Reports claimed that James' former teams, the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Miami Heat, were leading the charge to sign him. He was also heavily linked to the Golden State Warriors.

But James joins a 76ers team that has not won an NBA championship since 1983 and has not advanced out of the second round of the Eastern Conference playoffs since 2001.

Philadelphia fans will be hoping he can wipe out that streak just as he did in Cleveland, who had not won a title for 52 years before he led them to success in 2016.

The Athletic reports that Maxey and other key figures with Philadelphia have been relentlessly pursuing James in recent weeks. Their blockbuster trade for Brown with the Celtics also tipped the balance in their favor.

James, who will turn 42 in December, is about to enter his 24th season in the NBA, which is a league record. He is the all-time leading scorer in NBA history and has won four championships, two with the Heat and once each with the Cavaliers and Lakers.

Sports.title: Idrissa Gana Gueye set to leave Everton for Saudi Arabia, Aston Villa in talks to sign another Chelsea outcast after Alejandro Garnacho - as Maxence Lacroix has Blues medical ahead of £55m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Idrissa Gana Gueye set to leave Everton for Saudi Arabia, Aston Villa in talks to sign another Chelsea outcast after Alejandro Garnacho - as Maxence Lacroix has Blues medical ahead of £55m move: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Arsenal signing Christos Tzolis in a £34million move from Club Brugge - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Garner's a no-go as Everton dig in their heels

Everton insist James Garner is not for sale despite mooted interest from Premier League rivals.

The midfielder signed a new contract last season and was rewarded for his form with a call-up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad.

Aston Villa, Newcastle United and his former club Manchester United have all been linked in recent months but Everton have no desire to sell with the 25-year-old a key part of David Moyes's plans.

A string of Premier League clubs have been linked with James Garner, 25

Como set to increase bid for Chalobah

Como are expected to hold talks with Chelsea tomorrow over an improved offer for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The England centre back is keen on making the move and the Italians - managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas - have indicated they would increase their bid closer to Chelsea's valuation of £35million including add ons.

Como have so far proposed £25m.

For more on this story click HERE

Gana Gueye leaving Everton for big-money Saudi deal

Idrissa Gana Gueye is poised to take up a lucrative offer to play in Saudi Arabia.

The 36-year-old has now abandoned talks over a new contract with Everton and as a free agent is in the throes of finalising terms to move to the Saudi Pro League, joining Al-Diriyah.

The Senegal international also had interest from ambitious French side Le Havre but key to his decision apart from the financial gain is a desire to bring up his children in a Muslim country.

Gueye was popular figure at Everton but turns 37 in September.

David Moyes was willing to offer a new contract but wants more energy in his midfield. He has signed Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough and wants two more for his engine room.

Idrissa Gana Gueye joined Everton in 2022 and has made 120 league appearances for them

Lacroix closes in on £55m Chelsea move

Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today after the Blues agreed a deal for the Crystal Palace defender worth around £55m on Thursday.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace and France star Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today

Villa in talks to sign Jackson

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson.

The clubs have already agreed a loan with obligation deal for Alejandro Garnacho to join Villa. That followed the £117m sale of Morgan Rogers.

The structure of the deals are key as Chelsea and Villa are among those that need to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio regulations and their 2025 settlement agreements.

Rogers' £117m move will provide Villa with a significant accounting profit, potentially over £80m after Middlesbrough's sell-on clause and the remaining book value of his 2024 signing are deducted.

But if Chelsea had sold Garnacho to Villa as part of the same transaction, Uefa would treat it as a swap deal, impinging on profit margin. Even if Garnacho left on deadline day September 1, that is fewer than the guideline of 45 days, making it harder to argue they are not connected.

A loan with an obligation to buy could still be regarded as part of a swap deal because the 'purchase' has been agreed within 45 days of Rogers' transfer but the conditions give Villa control of when that deal is completed and potential room for manoeuvre with Uefa regulators.

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson

Summerville's Saudi switch confirmed

Al-Hilal have confirmed the signing of winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham in a deal worth up to £60million.

The 24-year-old, who also had an offer from Roma, had a medical in Amsterdam on Tuesday.

Al Hilal will pay an initial fee of £55m, plus £5m in potential add-ons.

Magpies get their man

Aladji Bamba will wear the number eight shirt vacated by Sandro Tonali, after completing his £30million move to Newcastle United.

Bamba arrived from Monaco on Thursday and Newcastle will pay a further £5.5m in add-ons.

The 20-year-old has signed a five-year contract and manager Eddie Howe said: 'He's another exciting, young signing who we're really looking forward to working with.

'Aladji adds depth and a range of qualities to our midfield options, with a huge potential for growth.

'His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and something we believe we can help him build on.

'He operates in a deeper role but has the ability to contribute all over the pitch, which he demonstrated in both Ligue Un and the Champions League last season.'

Meanwhile, Newcastle say they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

No Blues interest in Bruno

Chelsea are not expected to pursue a move for Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

There had been suggestions that the West London club were interested in the Brazilian international, but Chelsea sources categorically refute this.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Chelsea have not, at any point, enquired about Guimaraes and sources maintain they have no plans to.

BOBBY MANZI

Ex-Burnley star catching Tigers' interest

Hull City are interested in Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis.

The Portuguese was on loan from Benfica last season, but Burnley have just made that move permanent for £20million as their obligation from the original deal.

However, Burnley are also understood to be willing to sell the 26-year-old to recoup funds and salary while they are in the Championship.

Boro target World Cup star

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA midfielder Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps.

Boro are paying £900,000 for the 25-year-old who has 18 caps and played in all of the USA's World Cup games.

The deal includes a further £600,000 in add-ons.

Berhalter was born in London where his father Gregg, a former USA coach, was a player at Crystal Palace.

Boro remain in talks for left-back Max Arfsten from Columbus Crew also.

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto is understood to be among the names on Manchester City's radar as they formulate a list of potential wing targets.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games heat plunged into chaos with star's appearance delayed by 10 minutes - before volunteer strips off to save the day
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games heat plunged into chaos with star's appearance delayed by 10 minutes - before volunteer strips off to save the day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games return was marred by a bizarre delay which held him back from the pool for 10 minutes.

The swimmer, who has added his wife Holly's family surname to his own, made a splash in the 100m breaststroke heats.

Ramsay-Peaty recorded the quickest time of anybody in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals this evening, with the final being tomorrow.

But the 31-year-old, who is targeting a fifth Commonwealth gold medal, had to wait around due to a strange occurrence.

While he was on the blocks, one of the lane dividers broke off, leading to some commotion as the fixing had sunk to the bottom of the pool.

Fortunately, a volunteer was on hand to strip down to his shorts and dive in to amend the problem.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty (not pictured) was delayed on his return to the Commonwealth Games... as a volunteer had to jump in the pool to fix a lane line

The swimmer blasted through his 100m breaststroke heat and is hoping for a fifth Commonwealth gold

Holly Ramsay cheered husband Adam on from the sidelines amid her pregnancy

And none of that put Ramsay-Peaty off his stride as he blasted to a time of 59.46 seconds.

This is his fourth Commonwealth Games – his debut was in 2014 in Glasgow, and he has made the tournament a happy hunting ground with four golds and three silvers.

Alongside the 100m, the three-time Olympic champion will also partake in the 50m breaststroke event.

His wife, Holly, the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay, shared a snap to her Instagram Stories of Adam in his new 'Ramsay-Peaty' swimming cap and wrote: 'So Special.'

Holly, a 26-year-old influencer, is pregnant with their child.

Swimmer Ramsay-Peaty's parents did not attend the wedding in December and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail revealed that Adam's pregnant sister Bethany – the only member of his family to still be in contact with the couple – has now sensationally fallen out with Holly.

The roots of the family conflict go back to September 2024, when Adam and Holly snubbed wider members of the Peaty family by not inviting them to their engagement party.

Holly shared a snap to her Instagram Stories of Adam in the new swimming cap and wrote: 'So Special'

The athlete duly wasted no time in recording the fastest time of the morning, 59.46 seconds

Influencer Holly, 26, announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam

His parents, Caroline and Mark, did not attend the wedding and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them

Mother Caroline, who spent years ferrying her son to early-morning training sessions, was also not invited to Holly's glamorous hen do at Soho Farmhouse in the Cotswolds, even though the bride's mother, Tana, and friends including Victoria, were at the extravagant bash.

Adam changing his name to Ramsay-Peaty and registering under the double-barrel surname for the Games in Glasgow is seen by some as the latest blow for his estranged loved ones – especially as Ramsay is placed first before Peaty.

A source said previously: 'Adam may be rich but we have something that he doesn't and that is brains, loyalty, integrity and family.

'Money makes for a cold bedfellow. It can't hold you tight when things go wrong or when you have a bad day.'

They added: 'When you live to be famous you aren't living, you are playing a role. Fame is fleeting but family is forever.'

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

A silver medal at the Paris Olympics in 2024 helped him refocus after a difficult 2023 in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns.

He credits his Christian faith with saving him and helping him turn his life around.

His win in the 100m in 2014 began eight years of almost total dominance in the event. That streak came to an end in dramatic fashion in Birmingham four years ago when he trailed home in a shock fourth place in the event.

The athlete, who is due to return for his semi-final on Friday evening, told TNT Sports: 'Job done, really. We've got a busy two weeks coming up, so we're reserving energy where we can.

'Last time I was here, I was very young. We barely had any world records to my name, or known world records to my name, so it's been a very long journey.'

Sports.title: Liverpool flop Loris Karius opens up on nightmare fallout after Champions League final horror show - and admits he nearly QUIT after his career 'suddenly crashed to rock bottom'
Sports.content:
Former Liverpool goalkeeper Loris Karius has finally broken his silence on the nightmare fallout following his costly mistakes in the Anfield club's 3-1 Champions League final defeat to Real Madrid in Kyiv.

The 33-year-old first gave the ball to Madrid striker Karim Benzema with a wayward pass, with the Frenchman slotting into an empty net. Later, he flapped at a Gareth Bale strike, handing victory to the Spaniards.

That disastrous performance spelt the end of his Liverpool career and has followed him for the subsequent years of his career. But last season the German redeemed himself at current club Schalke, helping seal the club's return to the top-flight – keeping 13 clean sheets in Bundesliga two conceding only 24 goals in 30 matches.

Now, he has publicly spoken about 'hitting rock bottom' after that dreadful night in Kyiv had on his mental health and his career. Speaking to the Funke Media Group, Karius said: "Up until that point, my career had been on a steep upward trajectory, then I suddenly crashed – all the way to rock bottom.”

"It was extremely tough, partly because, in my mid-twenties at the time, I wasn't as grounded as I am now. And quite honestly, during that period I lost my love for football. I no longer wanted to train, I no longer wanted to play.

“At times, I struggled to go into work and just tried to get through the day in a somewhat normal way.”

Loris Karius has opened up on his nightmare performance in the 2018 Champions League final

Karius 'hit rock bottom' after his display in Kyiv but has bounced back in style with Schalke

The German's wife, Diletta Leotta, praised her husband's mental fortitude earlier this year

Karius' revelation offered a glimpse into the mental turmoil that can trouble footballers. Following his Liverpool exit, the 33-year-old struggled at Union Berlin and Newcastle before finding a home in Schalke. Karius reflected that perspective on his achievements thus far have helped him appreciate his position as a top-level footballer.

“Who else can say they play in front of 60,000 fans every other week? Only absolute superstars in the music industry can achieve that – you have to keep reminding yourself of that."

Karius' sobering account of his troubling experience follows comments made by his wife, DAZN TV presenter Diletta Leotta, praising her husband's determination and resilience.

She took to Instagram following Schalke's promotion, writing: is sport can be tough, sometimes ruthless. [It] exposes you, tests you, makes you fall in front of everyone.

'But if you find the strength to stay, to believe again, sooner or later it brings you back exactly where you deserve to be.

'I have seen that strength up close. In the silences, in the difficult moments, on the days when it would have been easier to give up.

'And today it's not just a victory. It's a revival. It's love for what you do. That's courage. Proud of you.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca vows not to let Man City crumble like at Man United when Sir Alex Ferguson left as he delights at sealing Man City return to replace Pep Guardiola following Chelsea exit
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca says it’s a privilege to succeed Pep Guardiola as Manchester City manager and is confident the empire he built won’t collapse like it did at Manchester United when Sir Alex Ferguson retired.

Guardiola won 20 trophies during his decade in charge at the Etihad before deciding to walk away at the end of last season. Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant and City’s elite development system coach during his two previous stints at the club, is relishing the chance to succeed him.

The 46-year-old Italian believes he can maintain City’s success because the club has been so well run under Guardiola, Manuel Pellegrini and Roberto Mancini, and there is no danger of a slump as United and Arsenal suffered when Ferguson and Arsene Wenger left.

‘I have to say that it's a privilege, because the reason why the club decided to go for me means that for me it's a privilege,’ said Maresca at his official unveiling on Friday.

‘I consider Pep probably the best coach in the world in the last 20-25 years. But again, it's a challenge. It's nice. It's a privilege. Also, the history of the manager with many years in the same club, always struggling a bit afterwards, after Sir Alex and after Arsene. It's a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.

‘I think the organisation is the main thing. This club, this organisation, they had three managers in 17 years. This is not normal. It does not happen often. So this probably is one of the things that I'm confident why we can do a great job. We can continue to do the job that has been done in the last probably 14, 15 years since Roberto was here, Mancini, then after Manuel for 10 years Pep.’

Enzo Maresca was unveiled to the media as Manchester City boss on Friday

Maresca succeeded Pep Guardiola as City boss, signing a three year deal at the Etihad

Maresca was reluctant to be drawn on his departure from Chelsea in January which ended with City paying their Premier League rivals £17million in compensation after they appointed him as Guardiola’s successor.

‘I have been quite lucky in terms of my former clubs, Leicester and Chelsea,’ added Maresca, who won the Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League at Stamford Bridge. ‘I think we did a great job in both clubs. The identity of the team was clear. The success of the team was clear, and I feel very lucky to be part of these clubs. But now I think we are here today. That is the most important thing. Just about City. Nothing to add.’

The new manager was asked about City midfielder Rodri who continues to be linked with a move to Real Madrid after entering the final year of his contract at the Etihad. The Spaniard is due to undergo surgery on a back injury after winning the World Cup earlier this month.

‘First of all, we have to say that around big players, there are always speculations,’ said Maresca. ‘I'm not worried about that, I think it's normal. Also, because they won the World Cup, he was the best player or one of the best players.

‘I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he's a top player. But (he will have) surgery on Monday, and he needs a holiday. He needs to rest. He needs to recover, and then he will be back here with us.’

"I think every manager wants to have Rodri"



Enzo Maresca gives an update on Rodri following Spain's win in the World Cup 💬 pic.twitter.com/xsotBmJ2Ro — Sky Sports News (@SkySportsNews) July 24, 2026

Maresca is a disciple of Pep Guardiola, having worked as his assistant for their treble-winning season in 2022-23

He was also asked about the futures of goalkeeper James Trafford, who has been linked with Leeds, and Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Everton.

‘I know James because he was my keeper when I was with the Under-23s,’ replied Maresca. ‘So I know James very well. But again, it's when the transfer window is open, now and in January, anything can happen. So we’ll see. But at the moment, he’s one of our keepers.

‘Jack, at the moment, this year, he's Man City player. I always said the same. In any club I join, if there are players that belong to the club it's my duty to try to coach them.

‘I have a good relation with Jack. Since I left we kept in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and is a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens.’

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp confirmed as Germany manager - and has already threatened to QUIT after World Cup's 'most controversial WAG' was criticised: 'If you don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jurgen Klopp has been unveiled as Germany manager – and has already revealed what will make him quit the job.

The Liverpool legend, 59, is back in the dugout having enjoyed a stint overseeing Red Bull's football operation after leaving Anfield in 2024, and has been tasked with turning the national team around after another disappointing major tournament.

Julian Nagelsmann was given his marching orders after the Germans crashed out to Paraguay in the Round of 32, leading to an inquest into the team's performance –where the players' WAGs and families were placed under the spotlight.

Nagelsmann's partner also made headlines, with German media reporting that his girlfriend, Lena Wurzenberger, was an almost constant presence in the camp.

But Klopp has already set his stall in a robust unveiling, insisting that he will quit the job immediately if his family face any scrutiny.

'The day you don't want me anymore, you say so and I'm gone, without severance pay,' he said via Bild.

'If you say tomorrow that he's rubbish, I'm gone. Not just one person, it would have to be more than that. If the DFB says he's rubbish, I'm gone. If you behave badly and don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone.'

Jurgen Klopp is Germany's new manager, but has already set out what will make him quit

Klopp says he will leave if the media 'don't leave my family in peace' after his predecessor Julian Nagelsmann's relationship with an ex-reporter made headlines

Klopp also described his appointment to the national team position as 'the highlight of my career'.

'Criticise me if something doesn't work. I'm happy to work on it. It's all about the job. Jurgen Klopp doesn't have a career after the national team. Ideally, this is the highlight of my career.'

Wurzenberger, 34, reportedly caused 'quite a stir' among the squad after being 'more present than probably any national team's coach before her'.

She was first spotted at Germany's pre-tournament camp in Frankfurt, when she was pictured watching training from a balcony along with a host of the players' partners.

And after her boyfriend's side thumped Curacao 7-1 - Wurzenberger hung around to watch the German substitutes complete their warm down.

It was then reported that she accompanied Nagelsmann back to the team hotel, before the duo were seen cycling to training together the following morning.

'There is naturally always that feeling that when the boss's wife is in the room, you might not always be completely honest at the table when talking about the national coach,' local reporters speculated during the tournament.

Klopp met second wife Ulla Sandrock in 2005 and married her that same year

Wurzenberger, and indeed Nagelsmann, also incited criticism from Germany legend Lothar Matthaus, who admitted her constant presence is far from 'ideal'.

The midfielder, who earned 150 caps, said on German television: 'She just shouldn't appear in the pictures too often - that wouldn't be ideal in my opinion.

'The players have days off and their families can come to the hotel. Lena (Wurzenberger) did that too. From my perspective, I think it's perfectly normal.

'Lena was able to come to the hotel just like the players' girlfriends and wives. You can see the solidarity - but the rule shouldn't apply to the coach. It has to happen during the time when we players are seeing their families.'

Nagelsmann and Wurzenberger are reported to have started dating soon after he split from his ex-wife Verena, following 15 years together, in 2022.

At that point Nagelsmann was manager of German giants Bayern Munich - and his new love interest reported on the club for Bild.

An article from the publication announcing their romance read: 'Julian Nagelsmann loves Bild reporter'.

Klopp married social worker and children's writer Ulla Sandrock in December 2005, having met at a pub during an Oktoberfest celebration that same year. He was previously married to ex-wife Sabine, with whom he shares a child.

Elsewhere, Arsenal legend Per Mertesacker will play an integral role in Klopp's transformation of the German national team, having been appointed the new Managing Director of Sport for the federation.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury fight LIVE RESULT from Anthony Joshua warm-up fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's blistering rant on the heavyweight division

Tyson Fury brutally did not hold back in his assessment of the current landscape of the heavyweight division.

Since Fury's return, the heavyweight division has changed immensely. Following Oleksandr Usyk's controversial stoppage win against kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven over in Egypt back in May, the Ukrainian decided to drop his three body belts - the WBA 'super', WBC and IBF - in a move which has sent shockwaves across the sport.

Murat Gassiev is the WBA champion, while Agit Kabayel is recognised as the WBC title holder. Daniel Dubois became a two-time world champion after knocking out Fabio Wardley back in May for the WBO strap, and the IBF belt remains vacant. Following the monumental shift, it now presents Fury with a perfect chance to become a three-time champion.

But when asked where he fits into the current picture in the blue ribbon division, Fury did not mince his words. "He does not. All those men have been gifted world titles. They never actually fought anyone to get one," he said on Wednesday. "Fabio Wardley - gifted a world title. Daniel Dubois - gifted a world title. Agit Kabayel - gifted a world title. Murat Gassiev - gifted a world title. How could you compare them men to me? Who's fought legends of the game and beat them for world titles.

"They're in their own little group, and I am f****** on top of the Empire State Building. They have got f*** all I want. They do not have any money. I have already had all the belts. They have got nothing that I want. And their names... they are not even high record names. Like, who knows who these people are? I know they are only just starting out their careers, most of them are a few years younger than me, but they are starting out with a no name and they have got to build their way up, and it's going to take years to get there.

"This Gassiev guy who has just won a world title, who knows that guy outside of Russia? Nobody. Agit Kabayel. Frank Warren said 'you can't fight him!' Back in 2020. 'You can't fight Agit, he's a no name. You'd get booed out the stadium.' He was only 24-0, number one rated in the IBF at the time. All these guys, they are all doing their thing. They are all going to fight it out between themselves. Even after being retired for ten years, I can still come back and get a world title shot at any time, because I have paid the price. I have spent hours and years in this game to be able to do that. I will always be a big name."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury sets up Anthony Joshua fight as rival QUITS on his stool
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury sets up Anthony Joshua fight as rival QUITS on his stool

Tyson Fury took on Mariusz Wach on Friday, 24 hours before Anthony Joshua takes to the ring for his own warm-up clash ahead of the all-British heavyweight showdown

View Image Tyson Fury celebrates

Tyson Fury stopped Mariusz Wach to uphold his end of his bargain with Anthony Joshua.

‌



Fury was fighting for the second time this year having outpointed Arslanbek Makhmudov in London in April. He had insisted on a second warm-up bout before he takes on Joshua in November - and Fury made no mistake against 46-year-old Polish veteran Wach in Thailand on Friday.

‌



Fury now faces a nervous wait for Joshua to take to the ring in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night against Kristian Prenga. Victory for the Olympic champion should see a date and venue finally announced for the all-British heavyweight showdown.

‌



Fury, who was fighting in front of 1,500 fans and donating all ticket proceeds to a children's charity, began patiently, feinting with his jab before turning southpaw. He continued in that stance through the second round as Wach ate four jabs in succession before firing back with a right hand. Fury then landed a three-punch combination after the ball and is forced to apologise.

Fury continued to switch between stances in the third round as Wach began to tire. The Pole was content to lean on Fury having outweighed the Brit at Friday's weigh-in. Fury continued to jab his way through the fight while playing to the crowd in the fourth session.

Article continues below

Wach reminded Fury he was still in the fight with a solid right hand in the fifth round. Fury responded by pinning the Pole in the corner and firing off his uppercut to leave Wach feeling the pace by the halfway mark.

And after appearing leggy in the seventh round, Wach was checked over by the doctor and after a brief discussion with his team, the fight was waved off.

More to follow...

Sports.title: Kia Joorabchian issues vote of confidence in jockey David Egan saying he ‘needed a break’
Sports.content:
Kia Joorabchian issues vote of confidence in jockey David Egan saying he ‘needed a break’

Questions were asked about Egan’s position with Amo Racing after Rossa Ryan rode a double for the team in Ireland at the weekend

View 2 Images Kia Joorabchian: backed David Egan (Image: Tattersalls)

Kia Joorabchian has issued a vote of confidence in Amo Racing’s contracted jockey David Egan.

‌



Questions were raised about Egan’s position within the ambitious football agent’s team after he was not in the saddle when two horses ran at the Curragh last weekend. Rossa Ryan, Egan’s predecessor with Amo, rode instead and was successful on both Robson De Aguiar-trained runners, notably in the Group 2 Minstrel Stakes.

‌



Without immediate clarification from Amo, online bookmaker Betway offered odds of 4-1 about Frankie Dettori, who has been an ambassador for the team since retiring in February, riding for the owners in the UK before the end of 2027.

‌



Chelmsford racecourse saved after takeover with racing close to returning READ MORE :

While Dettori laughed off the suggestion, Egan said: “There’s been no quotes from anyone and I’d like to say no comment from me.

“I’ve got no comment on the situation. I’m declared to ride a horse on Friday for Amo, plan to ride for him on Saturday and even into next week so no comment.”

Egan and Joorabchian were together at Ascot where the Amo-owned, Charlie Fellowes-trained Treasurer finished seventh of ten in the Listed Pat Eddery Stakes.

‌



Before the race Joorabchian spoke for the first time about the situation to Sky Sports Racing.

View 2 Images David Egan: staying in Amo Racing job

He said: “Rossa Ryan still rides for me, Kevin Stott rode for me this year and David has been part of our team for two and a half years.

‌



“We treasure him very much. He’s a very, very important part of the team. Regardless of what people think of the operation and what he is, he means a lot to us.

“He’s been to America for us, he’s been all over the world for us and he will continue, hopefully, to have a very, very successful season for us. If people want to make stories about us because it suits them, that suits them.”

Asked why Ryan rode the horses in Ireland, he said: “Because that was outside the country. He had ridden all week, he had been very tired, I felt he was very tired. I felt he needed a small break and I think a break would have done him well. I wanted him to come back refreshed.

Article continues below

“Why? Because we have Goodwood, we have York, we have multiple races.”

He added: “Egan is my man, he’s always been my man. It doesn’t mean we don’t have a right to give someone a break or a rest for a day.”
