World.title: Tallinn Airport downplays impact if airBaltic cuts routes
World.content:
The Latvian state airline airBaltic may soon face bankruptcy or route cuts due to financial difficulties. Tallinn Airport says it sees no reason for panic if its largest carrier leaves.

AirBaltic is the airline with the largest market share in Tallinn, used by nearly one‑third of all passengers. The company serves almost 30 routes from Tallinn Airport.

The airline's difficulties have reached the point where Tallinn routes are threatened with closure.

The company's loss exceeded 44 million euros last year. This year Latvia gave airBaltic a short‑term loan of 30 million euros, with a repayment deadline of 31 August. The closer the deadline approaches, the bigger the question mark over whether the struggling airline can repay the loan.

If the airline does not repay the money received from the state on time, the European Commission will treat it as state aid and will very likely initiate proceedings.

Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs. Source: Riigikogu

Latvian Finance Minister Māris Kučinskis admitted publicly in early July that airBaltic will likely have to reduce operations due to financial difficulties.

Lithuania announced that it is already preparing a backup plan in case airBaltic reduces its operations or leaves the country due to financial problems.

Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said last week that the government is negotiating with a major investor to save the airline. The prime minister admitted that the purpose of involving an investor is to avoid the risk of insolvency.

Riigikogu member and aviation expert Toomas Uibo (Eesti 200) commented on Friday that finding a major investor would bring Tallinn Airport the same result as the airline's bankruptcy — the investor is likely not interested in the airline flying from Tallinn.

Toomas Uibo. Source: ERR

"If a major investor were to come into airBaltic now, they would naturally review all routes and the entire strategy the company has developed over recent decades. These reorganizations could be very large. AirBaltic's primary task or interest is naturally to maintain Riga as its main base on which the route network is built," Uibo said.

Uibo noted that in addition to tourism routes, the airline also serves business routes, and their interruption would be felt in Estonia's economy.

Tallinn Airport is not preparing separate plans

Tallinn Airport board member Eero Pärgmäe said the airport has 15 regular carriers, which ensures that if something happens to one of them, people can continue flying because other carriers will fill the gap.

He noted that Tallinn Airport has several hub airports, and airBaltic also flies several routes in parallel with another airline, meaning the market cannot end up in a situation where people lose flight options.

Eero Pärgmäe. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

"Tallinn Airport is a company, and every company must assess its risks. Naturally, we have assessed the risks related to airBaltic. We have made the necessary calculations and plans. But at the moment we do not see a major reason for panic. AirBaltic continues to operate on all routes, and we are in constant contact with them. And we very much hope that their restructuring plan proceeds successfully," Pärgmäe said.

Pärgmäe noted that Tallinn Airport already has a route‑support program that includes discounts for new routes, and if needed, the airport can make it even more attractive. "When an airline opens a new route, it pays a lower price for certain years," he explained.

AirBaltic's departure would affect smaller routes

Aviation expert Erki Urva said airBaltic's departure would be a major blow for Estonia, but at the same time a relief for Latvian taxpayers, who have so far subsidized flights from Estonia.

"They have paid for all this subsidy in millions or almost billions of euros with which the Latvian state has supported airBaltic's operations here, in Lithuania and elsewhere," he said.

Other airlines likely could not take over all routes.

"I suspect that marginal routes will disappear. Competitors are more interested in carrying passengers through their hub airports — for example, Finnair through Helsinki, Lufthansa through Frankfurt, and LOT certainly through Warsaw. They will simply add capacity there, but I do not believe that direct flights will return in large numbers," he said.

Erki Urva. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"To some destinations, flights will certainly continue with low‑cost carriers, such as Wizz Air, Ryanair or someone else," Urva noted.

While Lithuania is already preparing a backup plan, Urva said Estonia does not appear to have political readiness to invest in aviation again.

"There has been talk that tens of millions have been burned through Estonian Air and Nordica. I do not agree with that claim and am completely convinced that Estonian aviation companies have brought more money into the Estonian state than has gone out, through export revenues, tax revenues and similar. But at present I do not see anyone in Estonia seriously considering creating a third state‑owned airline," he said.

Estonian state has no direct backup plan

Lithuania is preparing a backup plan in case airBaltic significantly reduces flights from Vilnius or shuts down entirely.

Kuldar Leis. Autor/allikas: Priit Mürk/ERR

"We are in a very, very similar situation to Lithuania, and our backup plan has actually been underway for quite some time, because airBaltic's market share in Estonia has decreased. Tallinn Airport has done a very good job replacing and finding new carriers and routes. From the airport's perspective, everything is proceeding normally," said Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform Party).

The government does not plan to stop requesting dividends from Tallinn Airport, which would allow the airport more resources to support routes.

"Dividends can be discussed when the time comes. Today Tallinn Airport has managed so well that the number of routes is increasing and they can also pay dividends. The priority is increasing air traffic, and dividends come second, so things are proceeding in the right order. There is no need to give up dividends now," Leis said.

Estonia is awaiting Air Baltic's new business plan

"From Estonia's side, we very much hope that airBaltic continues its operations and that its main owner — the Latvian state — continues to lead and support the airline so that it can continue operating. As we hear, they are preparing yet another new business plan on how to shrink sustainably. We would also like to see what airBaltic's future looks like according to the new business plan," Leis said.

Although "shrinking sustainably" would clearly mean reducing routes in Estonia as well, the infrastructure minister expressed hope that the company will nevertheless survive.

An airBaltic jet. Source: AirBaltic

World.title: Estonian women's choir brings home Singapore festival win
World.content:
Tallinn women's choir Kevad won first place in its category at the Singapore International Choral Festival (SICF), earning a gold award in the 10th edition competition.

The 27-member choir, led by conductor Õnne-Ann Roosvee, competed with works by Sergei Rachmaninoff, Tadeja Vulc and Estonian composer Veljo Tormis, including selections from his "Autumn Landscapes" suite.

Roosvee said Asian competitions have been especially successful for Kevad, which previously won at a choral competition in South Korea three years ago.

"I am extremely proud of our singers," she said. "This was the result of a great deal of teamwork, and we're incredibly happy."

Taking place July 16–20, SICF featured 73 choirs from 11 countries this year.

Named Estonia's women's choir of the year in 2020, Kevad celebrates its 20th anniversary in September.

The Nõmme-based choir brings together singers ages 18 to 63 with a shared passion for choral music, local acommunity involvement and continued growth.

World.title: Australia simplifies Estonian driving license exchange process
World.content:
Estonian drivers will soon be able to exchange their driving licences for Australian permits under a simplified procedure without taking a new test, the Ministry of Climate

The new procedure will take effect at the end of this year after a decision by the Australian road and transport authority, Austroads.

The change will allow Estonian drivers to exchange their driving licence for an Australian licence without taking additional tests.

"For Estonians moving to Australia to live, study or work, this will mean less bureaucracy, while the decision is also recognition of the quality of our driver training," said Sander Salmu, deputy secretary general for mobility at the Ministry of Climate.

Estonia was previously part of Australia's experienced driver recognition scheme, which allowed drivers over the age of 25 to obtain an Australian driving licence without taking local tests.

Last year, Australia decided to abolish the experienced driver exemption and invited the countries covered by the scheme to apply for a new, broader recognised-country status.

The new status expands the recognition of Estonian driving licences and no longer ties the simplified exchange procedure to the previous minimum age requirement of 25.

As implementing the recognition requires local regulations to be amended across Australia's states and territories, Estonia's new status will take effect at the end of 2026.

World.title: Russia orders Yandex Maps to blur military and strategic sites near Estonia's border
World.content:
About a year ago, large blurry patches appeared in Russia's Yandex Maps application. In the western part of the country alone there were 120 of them.

Eesti Ekspress, together with Norway's NRK and Sweden's SVT, investigated what Russia wants to hide. Blurred, for example, are the entire area of the Pskov airfield, the Olenya airfield in Murmansk oblast, the Kirishi oil refinery in Leningrad oblast, various research institutions, and radar and air‑defense points across Russia.

"The selection of blurred areas reflects the current capabilities of Ukrainian drone attacks," notes Estonian security expert Rainer Saks.

Rainer Saks. Source: ERR

Looking at the images, Saks concludes that these are largely places that are even worth attacking with drones. Since drones are fairly small aircraft that must travel long distances, the explosive payload they can carry is quite limited.

"It stands out that these are not only military objects but also critical infrastructure," says Villiko Nurmoja, founder of the defense‑industry company SensusQ and a long‑time military intelligence professional.

"Clearly, the aim is to protect themselves from becoming targets for Ukrainians, as these objects are important to the state and are considered specific targets, and a separate question is whether some objects have been placed there deliberately for deception."

Riho Ühtegi Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Estonian retired Major General Riho Ühtegi notes that hiding critical infrastructure is nothing new for Russia, since the same was done already in Soviet times, when large white patches appeared on public maps around military units and major factories.

"But even then satellites already existed, and it was known that the enemy had eyes in the sky that could not be evaded. Therefore things were hidden from their own citizens — to complicate possible espionage and sabotage," Ühtegi tells Eesti Ekspress.

Similarly, Ukrainians now have access to detailed Western satellite images as well as their own and allies' intelligence information, so they do not even need Yandex images.

Confusing choices for blurring

Norwegian NRK notes that there are many apparent contradictions among the 120 blurs.

"Multiple sources comment that it is hard to see any logic behind the way the locations are selected. For instance, some nuclear power plants are blurred, but not all of them. Also, some refineries, some naval bases, and some radar installations are blurred — but many are not."

In another place, the map blur does not cover an actual nuclear site but covers the related support facilities.

This blur is on the east coast of Lake Valdai and hides there the favorite resort of Putin and his two sons, according to reports, adds NRK. In comparison, the Google Maps app shows the same area with much clearer resolution.

In Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, next to Lithuania, there is a base station for the Russian satellite navigation system. It is completely blurred on Yandex maps but clearly visible on Google.

Pixelating online maps a relatively new phenomenon

Yandex Maps began blurring images inside Russia relatively recently: back in 2018, there was not a single blurred area, writes Sweden's SVT. "On December 24, 2024, a court in Moscow ruled that Yandex must mask the Ryazan oil refinery after it was attacked several times by Ukraine."

Intelligence officials from Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland believe that the expansion of Russian bases and the reinforcement of troops along the borders with Northern Europe and the Baltic could drag NATO and the Russian Federation into a dangerous confrontation, SVT adds.

"According to sources in the Danish intelligence services, these actions may indicate preparations for a potential large‑scale conflict with European states in the Baltic Sea region. [---] The sources emphasize that Russia has not yet made any confirmed decisions regarding aggression, but preparatory processes are already underway."

World.title: Construction of 2+2 section of Tallinn-Tartu highway begins in autumn
World.content:
Work on the Käsukonna–Imavere 2+2 road section on the national Tallinn–Tartu–Võru–Luhamaa highway will begin in September and is expected to take approximately 2.5 years.

The Transport Administration and KMG OÜ have signed a contract to build the 2+2 road section between kilometres 99.1 and 107.1

Janno Sammul, director of the Transport Administration's Road Maintenance Service, said the section is an important project for the agency that will make travel on the Tallinn–Tartu highway safer.

"The Tallinn–Tartu route will gain another eight-kilometre 2+2 section. In addition, travel towards Viljandi will become smoother than it is at present," he said.

In total, the Transport Administration will have a total of 53 kilometres of 2+2 highways under development over the coming years, with a total cost of €277 million, Sammul added.

The project aims to upgrade the existing road into a four-lane highway to improve traffic safety, increase road capacity and enhance driving comfort.

The works include the construction of eight kilometres of 2+2 highway between Tallinn and Tartu, as well as collector roads, a wildlife overpass, two bridges over the Navesti River, three overpasses, small wildlife tunnels, a noise embankment and noise barriers.

The connection to Imavere will be provided via the new Paia interchange.

A safe bus stop with a waiting area, parking and a pedestrian and cycling path connecting to the existing path in Imavere village will be built at the Imavere interchange.

The Transport Administration plans to begin work in September this year, with the construction period scheduled to last 30 months.

The project will be carried out by KMG OÜ in cooperation with joint bidder Infragreen OÜ.

The total cost of the works is €42.8 million, excluding VAT.

The project is co-financed by the European Union Cohesion Fund, which will cover 95 per cent of the cost.

World.title: Ukraine hits ‘Russia’s Amazon’ warehouses outside St Petersburg
World.content:
Saint Petersburg – Ukrainian drones Friday hit warehouses for Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries for a third time in six days, this time near Saint Petersburg, triggering a fire that sent smoke pouring over the historic city.

Kyiv has accused Wildberries — Russia’s largest online retailer often known as the Russian equivalent of Amazon — of storing drone parts and helping the Russian army.

Ukraine has targeted Saint Petersburg as it steps up long-range drone strikes on Russian energy, military and logistics sites in recent weeks, calling the attacks justified retribution for Moscow’s nightly drone and missile barrage of its cities.

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down some 571 drones overnight over more than a dozen regions and Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that Russia annexed in 2014 — one of the largest one-night barrages of the war.

In Saint Petersburg, an AFP reporter saw grey smoke rising into the morning sky over high-rise residential buildings in the city, President Vladimir Putin’s hometown that is more than 800 kilometres (500 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

Wildberries said two of its logistics facilities in Saint Petersburg and one in Simferopol, in Moscow-annexed Crimea, were hit.

“Rapid evacuation was carried out at all the warehouses … according to preliminary data, there are no casualties,” Wildberries CEO Tatyana Kim said on social media.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the surrounding Leningrad region said three people were wounded in the attack, which saw at least 59 drones fired towards Saint Petersburg.

It was the third overnight attack by Ukraine on Wildberries’ sites in the past week.

Last weekend, eight night-shift workers were killed in attacks on Wildberries sites that saw one of the company’s main warehouses outside Moscow burn to the ground.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alleged after the first attack that the facilities were used to “supply sanctioned components for drone production and navigation equipment.”

Hundreds of small businesses saw their inventories wiped out in the strike, triggering angry comments on social media.

Kyiv calls its strikes “long-range sanctions”, saying the attacks are justified retribution for Russia’s more than four-year offensive and nightly attacks on its cities.

The campaign has triggered nationwide fuel shortages and, Kyiv says, dented Russia’s financial war chest.

– ‘Escalation’ –

Columns of thick black smoke were still billowing into the sky from one of the factories hours after the hit, an AFP reporter saw.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spent the first years of the war trying to shield the population from the fall-out of his decision to launch the offensive on Ukraine.

But the strikes on oil refineries have triggered fuel shortages and big attacks near major cities have brought the dramatic visible consequences of the war into the homes of many Russians.

Firefighters and investigators had been deployed to the sites in Saint Petersburg as the blaze raged through the morning, Russian officials said.

Saint Petersburg’s Pulkovo airport suspended flights during the attack, resuming operations around 06:00 (0300 GMT), with around 50 departures disrupted.

Both Russia and Ukraine have escalated their long-range strikes in recent months.

Moscow’s forces have fired increasing numbers of ballistic missiles at Kyiv — killing dozens and ripping open apartment blocks.

US President Donald Trump has appeared to give his backing to Ukraine’s counter-attacks on Russia — calling the strikes “an escalation that can lead to an end”.

Washington’s attempts to mediate a peace deal between the warring sides have largely stalled with its own war on Iran raging.

The United Nations has reported a surge in civilian deaths in 2026, saying June was the deadliest month since mid-2022.

Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and tens of thousands of civilians have been killed since Russia launched its full-scale offensive in February 2022 — though there is no precise toll with neither side routinely revealing the number of their losses.

World.title: South Korean tycoon ordered to pay $644m in divorce
World.content:
Seoul – A South Korean court ordered an AI chip-manufacturing tycoon on Friday to make a trimmed-down $644 million divorce payment to his former wife.

Chey Tae-won, 65, is the chairman of the SK Group, which owns world-leading memory chipmaker SK hynix — a pillar of South Korea’s tech-led economy.

Seoul High Court in 2024 had told him to pay 1.38 trillion won ($940 million) to his ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong, daughter of a former South Korea president.

The sum — equal to more than $1 billion at the exchange rate at the time of the ruling — led local media to dub it the “divorce of the century”.

Chey appealed to the Supreme Court, which told the high court to reconsider its 2024 decision and led to the tycoon’s reduced divorce bill of 944 billion won ($644 million).

The settlement is not yet final, however, as either side may refer it back to the Supreme Court.

The acrimonious case centres on the definition and valuation of the couple’s shared assets, including Chey’s lucrative stake in the SK Group.

Seoul High Court ruled Friday that Roh was entitled to a cash payout worth one-third of the couple’s marital assets.

“The defendant’s shareholdings increased substantially during the marriage through his management activities,” the court said.

“The plaintiff contributed to that increase through homemaking, childcare and public-facing activities related to SK Group.”

Chey and Roh married in 1988, but the couple are believed to have lived apart for more than 15 years. In 2015 he admitted to fathering a child with his lover.

With SK hynix selling vital memory chips to AI computing company Nvidia, Chey’s stake is now worth roughly $5.5 billion, according to regulatory filings and public data.

Roh, 65, has three children with Chey and has built a career in the cultural space, running a digital art museum.

– Bribes –

The pair were wed in Seoul’s presidential Blue House when her father Roh Tae-woo led the country from 1988 to 1993.

They have battled over the split in the courts since 2022, after Chey filed for divorce in 2017 and mediation broke down.

The court’s original 2024 ruling ordering the payout to Roh cited a 30 billion won slush fund her ex-president father used to propel SK Group’s growth.

The court said at the time that could be counted as her contribution towards the couple’s shared assets.

But in October last year the Supreme Court quashed that argument, saying that any such cash likely stemmed from illegal bribes and therefore should not be counted.

Another question was whether the dramatic increase in SK Group’s value since the couple’s separation, on the cusp of the AI boom, should be reflected in the asset division.

“The court took into account the sharp rise in the value of the defendant’s shareholdings when determining the property division ratio,” Friday’s court statement said.

SK Group shares have more than tripled in value since December 2015, when Chey publicly disclosed his extramarital affair.

The Supreme Court had already separately ordered Chey to make an alimony payment to Roh of 2 billion won.

World.title: PepsiCo deepens Iraq partnership with manufacturing, agriculture deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – PepsiCo has inked agreements with two Iraqi partners to increase food and beverage production, boost agricultural supply chains, and create employment, adding to a string of US investments announced during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington.

The agreements, inked during the U.S.-Iraq High-Level Business Summit organized by the US Chamber of Commerce, strengthen PepsiCo’s collaborations with Baghdad Soft Drinks Company (BSDC), its long-standing bottling partner in Iraq, and Green Iraq Company (GICO).

According to the deal with BSDC, PepsiCo will aim to increase yearly production capacity to more than 250 million beverage cases, maintaining Iraq’s position as one of the company’s major manufacturing and bottling centers in the Middle East.

The expansion is planned to create new employment in manufacturing, engineering, logistics, and distribution, as well as teach and provide technical skills to Iraqi engineers and technicians.

A separate deal with GICO seeks to increase food production capacity and agricultural productivity by bringing advanced irrigation methods and farming practices to local farmers, therefore boosting Iraq’s goal to become a regional food and beverage export center.

According to PepsiCo, the program aims to boost domestic supply chains by encouraging more local procurement and assisting Iraqi farmers in improving yields and sustainability.

The deals were part of a series of commercial understandings struck at the summit, in which US and Iraqi firms announced commitments in energy, banking, aviation, infrastructure, and manufacturing as Baghdad strives to diversify its economy away from oil and attract foreign investment.

Baghdad Soft Drinks Company has been working with PepsiCo for over four decades, and both agreements were signed on behalf of BSDC and GICO by majority stakeholder Tarek Al Hassan.

The investment demonstrates global firms’ rising interest in Iraq’s consumer products industry, as improved economic circumstances and government reforms stimulate more private sector investment and industrial growth.

World.title: Socceroos star Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine
World.content:
Sydney – Australian World Cup star Cristian Volpato allegedly tested positive for cocaine after he was pulled over for speeding in Sydney on Friday, police and reports said.

A New South Wales police statement said a 22-year-old man — widely identified as Italy-based Volpato by local media — was allegedly caught speeding twice overnight.

He passed a roadside breath test on the first occasion and was issued an infringement notice before being pulled over again two hours later.

This time he was drug tested and returned a positive result for cocaine, police claimed, with a second sample sent for further analysis.

“His international driver’s licence was suspended for a period of six months, withdrawing his driving privileges in NSW,” police said.

Volpato, who plays for Serie A side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup after switching his international allegiance from Italy to Australia shortly before the tournament.

He was born and raised in Sydney before moving overseas and represented Italy at various youth levels.

Tony Basha, a Sydney-based coach who trained Volpato before he moved to Italy and remains a mentor, told the Sydney Morning Herald the attacking midfielder denied taking cocaine or any other illicit substance.

“He was adamant he didn’t touch it,” Basha said. “He was shocked. I’m shocked because it’s a big allegation.”

World.title: Volkswagen profit plunges as carmaker weighs mass job cuts
World.content:
Frankfurt – Volkswagen said Friday that its net profit plunged in the second quarter as the crisis-hit carmaker, weighing up to 100,000 job cuts worldwide, grapples with increasing competition in and from China.

Net profit for the three months to the end of June came in at 1.54 billion euros ($1.75 billion), the 10-brand group said, a fall of 32.9 percent on the same period last year. Last year’s figure was itself a decline of almost 37 percent on 2024.

The result was hit by a 500-million-euro charge the carmaker booked for stopping US production of its electric ID.4, Volkswagen said, as well as “negative mix effects”, meaning the automotive giant sold more lower-margin products.

The firm, which in addition to its own brand also includes the likes of Lamborghini, Audi, Skoda and Porsche, also cut its guidance for the year and said it now saw sales flat or falling up to three percent. It previously expected growth of up to three percent.

The results pile pressure on the beleaguered group, which has been suffering from slimmer margins from the sales of electric cars, US tariffs and above all intense Chinese competition.

“We must accelerate efforts to structurally lower our cost base and sustainably improve our earnings quality,” Volkswagen finance chief Arno Antlitz said. “What matters now is swift and consistent implementation.”

World.title: Iraq border in focus as Kuwait reports drone attack
World.content:
Dubai – Here are the main events related to the war in the Middle East:

– Iran blasts Trump assets threat –

Tehran said Friday that US President Donald Trump’s threat to pay for shipping damage with Iranian assets was an “incendiary precedent”.

Trump had said that Washington would start using frozen Iranian assets “that the United States has in its possession, and controls” to pay for “any and all damages done to Ships, Cargo or anything related” in the region.

– New US strikes –

The United States military said Thursday it was attacking Iran for the 13th night in a row, adding that strikes were aimed at military targets with the goal of diminishing Iranian ability to attack shipping.

Iranian state media reported that US missiles had hit the city of Ahvaz, near the border with Iraq, and explosions were heard in the port city of Bandar Abbas on the Strait of Hormuz and in Omidiyeh.

– Kuwait under attack –

Kuwaiti air defences have opened fire on incoming Iranian missiles and drones, hours after reporting a new drone attack at the border crossing with Iraq.

“Kuwaiti air defences are currently intercepting hostile missile and drone attacks following the wrongful Iranian aggression,” the general staff said in a message posted on social media.

– Trump rebuked –

The US House of Representatives passed a largely symbolic resolution calling for President Donald Trump to halt military action against Iran, delivering another congressional rebuke as the Middle East war escalates.

The measure directs Trump to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress explicitly authorises the war.

– Houthi attacks ‘illegal’ –

Attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea by Yemen’s Houthi militants have drawn condemnation from around Europe.

Germany said the attacks risked escalating conflicts, Britain condemned the group’s “reckless actions” and EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas said the attacks were “unacceptable” and “illegal”.

– UN chief warning –

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said the Middle East conflict was “getting out of control”.

“It is teetering on the edge of the unimaginable,” he said.

– Oil passes $100 –

The price of the benchmark international oil contract, Brent North Sea soared more than eight percent to reach $101.93 a barrel after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck oil tankers in the Red Sea.

The main US oil contract, West Texas Intermediate, rose 7.6 percent to $93.44 a barrel.

– Island strike –

Iranian news outlet Tasnim reported that a US missile had hit a site near the town of Suza on Qeshm Island, in the disputed Strait of Hormuz.

– Trump threatens Houthis –

Trump threatened Yemen’s Houthi rebels with “major military punishment” after they launched missile and drone strikes at oil tankers in the Red Sea.

“The US will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis themselves” should the rebels launch further attacks, Trump said on his Truth Social network.

– Britain withdraws Iran staff –

Britain said it had withdrawn remaining diplomatic staff from Iran.

“Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran. Our embassy continues to operate remotely,” the foreign ministry said on its website.

World.title: Kuwait blames Iran afters drones hit border with Iraq
World.content:
Kuwait City — Kuwait on Thursday said drones hit its side of the border with Iraq, with one Kuwaiti official telling AFP Iran was to blame.

“The Al-Abdali border crossing was attacked this afternoon by hostile drones, resulting in material damage, but thankfully no casualties,” defense ministry spokesman Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan said in a statement.

An Iraqi security source also confirmed the incident prior to the ministry’s statement.

World.title: Iraq, Iran sign transport, rail deals after Tehran talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq and Iran inked an agreement and three memorandums of understanding on transportation, rail connection, and government collaboration as Prime Minister Ali al-Falih al-Zaidi wrapped up an official visit to Tehran aimed at improving bilateral relations.

According to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s office, Al-Zaidi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and conducted extensive conversations with key Iranian officials such as Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Judiciary Chief Gholam-Hossein Mohseni Eje’i.

The two sides signed an agreement on international road freight transport and shipping, as well as memorandums of understanding to extend a railway connecting Kermanshah, Khosravi, Khanqin, and Baghdad, establish a twinning agreement between Baghdad and Tehran municipalities, and collaborate on government administration and human resource training.

Iraqi ministers in charge of foreign affairs, electricity, and finance, as well as the head of the Planning Commission, signed the agreements in the presence of Al-Zaidi and Pezeshkian.

The proposed railway extension would improve overland transportation links between Iraq and Iran, as part of Baghdad’s larger plans to expand regional trade corridors and improve cross-border connectivity through investments in rail, road, and logistics infrastructure.

The visit takes place as Iraq aims to retain tight economic and political connections with neighboring Iran while simultaneously developing partnerships with the United States and Gulf nations as part of a larger drive to diversify investment and boost regional cooperation.

According to the New York Times, Iran rejected a US cease-fire proposal delivered by Al-Zaidi during the visit, while Iraqi authorities made no public comment on the claim.

World.title: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident
World.content:
Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday condemned the attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping 'unacceptable' and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and global trade.The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.In a statement, the MEA said, "On 18 July 2026, the commercial vessel MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. At the time of the incident, there were ten crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. As per available information, one Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack. We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased. The other two Indian nationals on board are reported to be safe."Condemning the attack, the ministry said, "India unequivocally condemns such attacks targeting commercial shipping and placing the lives of innocent civilian crew members at risk.It is a matter of serious concern that the freedom of navigation and international commerce is facing increasing threats. India calls upon all concerned parties to uphold international obligations to ensure the safety and security of maritime navigation and uninterrupted flow of global commerce. "The latest attack comes after MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel, was struck shortly after departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on July 19. The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals. Four Indians were killed and one was critically injured in that attack.The MEA had then condemned the strike, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted, while assuring that India's mission in Ukraine was extending all possible assistance to those affected.The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, where renewed hostilities have increased risks to civilian vessels and global maritime trade.

World.title: Three chemical parks to be set up under BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA-Rasayan) scheme for establishing three dedicated chemical parks in the country.

The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, of which Rs 3,000 crore will be used for establishing common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities inside the parks, while the remaining Rs 30 crore has been earmarked for administrative expenditure.

Announced in the Union Budget, the scheme will run for five years. While the Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park, the state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.

Govt said the BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme is expected to promote the development of the chemical industry and its value chain, including upstream, downstream and ancillary industries, while ensuring efficient utilisation of resources.

By providing shared common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities tailored to the needs of the chemical industry, the scheme is expected to enhance cost competitiveness and make the Indian chemical industry globally competitive. It will also help the sector integrate better with global value chains, boosting exports and import substitution.

The scheme will create an environment-friendly ecosystem with centralised facilities such as a common effluent treatment plant, treatment, storage and disposal facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. Govt said the development of the chemical sector will generate employment and contribute to economic growth.

World.title: Government pushes competition in power distribution
World.content:
.

NEW DELHI: Union power ministryâs consultative committee met on Thursday to discuss a consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing that would allow multiple electricity suppliers to use the same distribution network.The proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider.The draft National Electricity Policy-2026, which is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon, has also underlined the need to phase out monopoly in electricity distribution and introduce competition by allowing multiple players.According to officials, the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, but requires each of them to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of infrastructure, higher capital expenditure, discourages fresh investment and leads to âinefficient utilisation of resourcesâ.Mumbai is the only city where consumers have exercised supplier choice for several years, while the distribution network is developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the state electricity regulatory commission.Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Union power minister Manohar Lal said consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecom and aviation. "Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure," the minister said at the meeting.Power ministry, in a statement, said members of Parliament who are part of the consultative committee offered valuable suggestions on the proposed framework. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks."New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned state electricity regulatory commission," govt said in the statement.

World.title: Creation and nurturing of society impossible without motherhood: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (

) chief

on Friday said motherhood is the foundation of creation, nurturing and continuity of society, asserting that "the creation, nurturing and sustenance of the world are impossible without motherhood.

"

Addressing the valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on "Contemporary Motherhood" organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha at the Ambedkar International Centre, Bhagwat said the core principles of motherhood remain timeless even as society changes.

He described mothers as a child's first teacher and the primary source of emotional support throughout life, saying they play a decisive role in shaping values and giving the right direction to a person's thinking.

Bhagwat said parents should spend more time with their families and maintain open communication with children. He stressed that children learn more through observation than instruction, making it important for parents to lead by example. He also said parents should continue to expand their own knowledge so they can address their children's questions and curiosity.

The RSS chief said many debates in society stem from misconceptions, some of which are deliberately created.





Referring to Indian culture, he said it had long been portrayed as flawed despite having a strong civilisational foundation. He urged people to move forward with confidence in India's history, traditions and knowledge systems.

He also said unity amid diversity lies at the heart of Indian culture and called for strengthening families and social institutions by following Indian cultural values rather than adopting foreign lifestyles without reflection.

Bhagwat began his address by saying it was somewhat paradoxical for him to speak on motherhood, adding that women have the primary authority to speak on the subject. He said the organisation had already held extensive discussions on the theme and noted that thinkers such as Swami Vivekananda, Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore had reflected extensively on motherhood and its relevance to society.

The event was organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha, a women's organisation that says it works towards "nation-building through motherhood."

The two-day meeting, held on July 23 and 24, brought together around 280 women from different states to discuss the role of motherhood in the context of changing social conditions and the Indian family system.

According to the organisers, more than 900 women attended the concluding session, while between 2,000 and 2,500 women had registered for the dialogue on the theme. The organisation said it held conventions across 23 regions in India in 2026, involving around 37,000 women, and is currently active in 33 regions with nearly six lakh women associated with its activities. It also has a presence in 14 countries, including the United States and the Netherlands.

World.title: 'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams critics after he ends 26-day hunger strike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Gitanjali Angmo on Friday came to the defence of her husband

's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike against the NEET paper leak, urging critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him.

In a post on X, Angmo said Wangchuk had "chosen sacrifice over comfort" and added that not everyone was qualified to judge a life dedicated to selfless service.

"Before you rush to criticise Sonam Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself," Angmo said.

"He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort. The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations.

Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart," she added.

This comes after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country.

In a separate post on X, Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of the two Union ministers and senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh Ladakh.





He added that 65 MPs from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast.

Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said it would continue its nationwide "peaceful protests" demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.

"The Cockroach Janata Party's peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a statement after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike.

World.title: NTA terminates 47 officials, begins specialist-led rebuild
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has terminated 47 officials and begun rebuilding its workforce with specialist leadership in cybersecurity, forensic investigation, test-centre operations and assessment research, government sources said on Friday.

Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies. More measures are expected as responsibility is fixed for failures in national entrance examinations.

The first phase includes four General Manager appointments and 16 Young Professionals through UPSCâs PRATIBHA Setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on Saturday, July 25, ministry sources said.

The crackdown follows the NEET-UG paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the examination again on June 21 after the May 3 test was cancelled. Sources stressed that the 47 personnel had been terminated, not merely transferred or marked for removal. Their names, ranks and alleged roles were not disclosed. Cases indicating criminal wrongdoing will be referred to the appropriate agencies, while departmental and legal proceedings will follow separately.





The four General Managers will be appointed on three-year contracts.

The assessment and psychometrics head will oversee question banks, normalisation, equating and calibration, and pilots on computer-adaptive testing and AI-assisted assessment.

The test-centre operations head will supervise

âs network across more than 500 cities and select overseas centres, including empanelment, capacity, accessibility, amenities, examination-day operations and coordination with administrations.

The information-security head will serve as Chief Information Security Officer, responsible for systems, networks, applications, candidate data, a round-the-clock Security Operations Centre and compliance with data-protection, information-technology and CERT-In requirements.

The vigilance, investigation and forensics head will lead malpractice inquiries, build in-house digital-forensics capability and coordinate with the CBI, Intelligence Bureau, Enforcement Directorate, state police and cybercrime units under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

NTA will also engage 16 Young Professionals through PRATIBHA Setu â Professional Resource And Talent Integration Bridge for Hiring Aspirants â for the first time. The platform gives verified employers access to willing candidates who cleared stages of UPSC examinations but were not recommended in the final merit list.

Twelve positions will be in academic research, two in legal research and two in finance and accounts.

Appointments will initially be for 24 months, extendable to 36 months based on performance.

The changes seek to reduce NTAâs dependence on temporary manpower. It has 39 sanctioned permanent posts, all on deputation, but only 24 are filled, against 73 contractual personnel and 124 outsourced workers.

Further hiring will follow across 10 functional verticals recommended by the Radhakrishnan committee. NTA has also initiated fresh empanelment of subject experts and translators.

The overhaul will accompany changes to examination delivery. NEET-UG will shift from OMR-based testing to computer-based testing from 2027, bringing it closer to JEE Main and CUET. The move should reduce physical movement of papers, enable multiple question sets and create a digital trail, but will require secure centres, stronger cybersecurity and safeguards against technical failures.

The government is also reviewing outsourcing in registration, centre management, technology services and handling of confidential material. The new model will define responsibility, strengthen audits and background checks, reduce agencies handling sensitive information and impose tougher penalties for security failures.

Sources said the reset would combine accountability for past lapses with safeguards against future leaks and malpractice.

World.title: Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers; President Murmu accepts resignation
World.content:
Bittu, a three-time former Congress MP from Punjab, was inducted as a minister of state in the Narendra Modi-led government in June 2024

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Friday accepted the resignation of Union minister of state for railways and food processing industries Ravneet Singh Bittu from the Union Council of Ministers with immediate effect, under Clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India.Bittu's resignation came after his Rajya Sabha tenure, representing Rajasthan, ended on June 21. He had been a member of the Upper House from August 2024 to June 2026.In a post on X, Bittu wrote, "I express my heartfelt gratitude to Honâble President Smt. Droupadi Murmu Ji and Honâble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji for giving me the opportunity to serve the nation as Minister of State in the Government of India. It has been an honour to serve the people of India, especially my beloved Punjab. I remain committed to the ideals of service, nationalism, and the vision of a Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Honâble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji. My journey of public service continues with renewed dedication."A three-time former Congress MP from Punjab, Bittu was inducted as a minister of state in the Narendra Modi-led government in June 2024 despite losing the Lok Sabha election from Ludhiana to Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring by 20,942 votes.He had joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in March 2024 ahead of the general elections after ending his long association with the Congress. Union Home Minister Amit Shah had projected Bittu as an important Sikh face for the BJP during the election campaign in Punjab.A grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, who was assassinated in 1995, Bittu represented Anandpur Sahib in the Lok Sabha in 2009 before winning from Ludhiana in 2014 and 2019. During his political career in the Congress, he also served as the party's leader in the Lok Sabha and as its whip in the Lower House.Bittu's resignation comes as the BJP prepares for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, which the party is expected to contest on its own after ruling out an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal.The BJP, which won only two seats in the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, is aiming to improve its performance in the state.

World.title: PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video amid NEET protest
World.content:
PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gained around 1 million Instagram followers overnight after he released his selfie video on Thursday night addressing concerns of the NEET paper leak.Currently PM Modi has 102 million followers on Instagram. His video captioned: "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrowâs Cabinet!" has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on Instagram.In the video, he announced that the government would introduce tougher measures to tackle examination paper leaks. He also informed about the Union Cabinet meeting agenda held on Friday."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians," he said."Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared amendments to the anti-paper leak law, proposing stricter punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks. Sources said the revised law prescribes up to 10 years in prison and a fine of as much as Rs 10 crore, while raising the minimum jail term from three years to five years.

World.title: Policeman who created ruckus at government hospital arrested, suspended
World.content:
Dindigul Superintendent of Police S. Jeyakumar on Friday ordered the suspension of a police constable attached to Kodaikanal police station, Thangapandi, who had created a ruckus at the government hospital in Kodaikanal.

It is said that Thangapandi visited the government hospital for treatment when he was off-duty. He was in civil dress. Following an altercation at the hospital with a nurse, the policeman created a ruckus at the place. He alleged that the nurse had addressed him in a disrespectful manner. It is said that he was under the influence of alcohol.

A case has been registered under the relevant sections of the BNS at Kodaikanal police station. Thangapandi was arrested and remanded in judicial custody. It is said that an appropriate departmental inquiry will be initiated and necessary action will be taken against the policeman.

World.title: Centre undertaking sweeping reforms to modernise India Post: Pemasani
World.content:
Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development Pemasani Chandra Sekhar on Friday said the Centre was implementing wide-ranging reforms to transform India Post into a world-class public service institution through technology, efficient leadership and a customer-centric approach.

Addressing a gathering after inaugurating the modernised Kothapet and Chandramouli Nagar Sub Post Offices in Guntur, he said India Post, with its presence in every village and household, would play a key role in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Describing the reforms introduced over the past two years as unprecedented, Dr. Chandra Sekhar said they had surpassed the changes seen over the previous two to three decades, demonstrating that public sector institutions could deliver world-class services with the right leadership and technology.

He said strengthening the department’s financial position remained a priority, as higher revenue would support employee welfare, modernisation and expansion of services. Annual postal revenue growth had increased from about ₹200 crore earlier to more than ₹2,100 crore in a single year following the reforms, he added.

Highlighting the department’s digital transformation, the Minister said nearly 80% of postal transactions in Andhra Pradesh were now conducted digitally, with India Post moving towards fully cashless post offices. Under the IT 2.0 initiative, savings and insurance services would be brought completely online, while Gen-Z post offices, dedicated mobile applications for employees and specialised training programmes would further improve service delivery.

Dr. Chandra Sekhar said India Post had expanded its logistics partnerships with ONDC, GeM, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and Patanjali, and was planning to collaborate with DHL to strengthen international parcel services. Features such as 24 to 48-hour parcel delivery, end-to-end tracking, SMS alerts, OTP-based delivery and geo-tagging were being introduced in phases.

He urged postal employees to promote savings, insurance and financial literacy at the household level and leverage the department’s extensive network to market products made by farmers, women self-help groups and small entrepreneurs across the country and overseas. He reiterated that the Centre aimed to make India Post the country’s most trusted, modern and people-centric public service institution.

World.title: Two M.P. Police constables arrested for raping minor dalit girl in Bhopal
World.content:
Two Madhya Pradesh Police personnel have been arrested for allegedly raping a minor Dalit girl after abducting her in Bhopal, police said on Friday (July 24, 2026).

According to the police, the incident took place on July 22 and that the minor survivor lodged a complaint in Bhopal’s Jahangirabad police station on July 23, based on which a case was registered.

Bhopal Additional Commissioner of Police (law and order) Shailendra Singh Chauhan told The Hindu that the accused have been identified as constables Santosh Sen and Jitendra Singh, and that the duo have been arrested.

“The complainant approached Jahangirabad Police Station and reported that two individuals, who are basically police constables, called the minor girl and took her in a car somewhere where one of them raped her,” Mr. Chauhan said.

Case registered

The officer said that a case under relevant provisions, including the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, and BNS Sections like 137(2), has been registered, and investigation has been taken up.

Mr. Chauhan said that a medical examination was conducted on the survivor.

Another officer from Jahangirabad said that the accused had called the girl and lured her on the pretext of taking her to someone’s birthday.

“They then took her to a secluded location where Santosh Sen raped her. After this they left the girl at a square in the city,” the officer said, requesting anonymity.

The officer said that the girl is currently at her home and her health condition is fine.

World.title: Strike by a section of online taxi operators continues in Kerala
World.content:
Most drivers attached to online taxi aggregator firms, barring a prominent online taxi-car platform, on Friday (July 24, 2026) evening decided to call off the indefinite ‘offline strike’ that the All Kerala Online Drivers Union Alliance (AKODUA) and other allied bodies had embarked on since July 21.

The app-based mobility platforms, mainly Kerala Savari and Rapido, have decided to resume services after the three-day strike, said Sajin Jose, a representative of the online drivers’ alliance. “With Uber not heeding the demands that we have persistently raised over the past decade, including reducing the percentage of commission levied on fares, it has now been decided that drivers will operate only through other mobility apps. Another round of talks will be held with the online platform’s officials next week, after which a decision will be taken on the ongoing strike,” he said.

The agitating drivers of around 30,000 online taxis, most of which operate in Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram, have also been seeking a fare revision in accordance with government norms, citing the increase in fuel prices, operation and maintenance expenses, and the ‘arbitrary’ locking of their IDs based on customer feedback. Online autorickshaws, however, have continued to operate.

Online Taxi Drivers’ Union president Sahir K.T. confirmed that member drivers had been instructed to switch on all mobility apps except Uber. “We are also reaching out to non-member drivers to spread awareness about the decision to go ahead with the offline strike against the platform,” he said.

World.title: SC proposes special courts for speedy trial in Manipur violence cases
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (July 24, 2026) proposed the establishment of special courts to conduct day-to-day trials in cases arising out of the 2023 Manipur violence and directed the investigating agencies to expedite the pending probes to ensure that there is no further “inordinate delay”.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing a batch of petitions relating to the ethnic violence in the State. Referring to status reports filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Special Investigation Team (SIT), the Bench noted that the prevailing law and order situation had made the examination of witnesses difficult, with many having been displaced or relocated.

The court also pointed out that the prolonged suspension of internet services had impeded the collection of digital evidence, while restrictions on the movement of investigating officers had hampered field investigations, contributing to delays in the probe.

“We tentatively propose to constitute special courts, with the concurrence of the State of Manipur and the High Courts of Manipur and Gauhati, for trials to be taken up on a day-to-day basis, especially in light of the inordinate delay that has already taken place in the ongoing investigation,” the Bench said.

To facilitate the establishment of the proposed special courts, the Bench directed Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the State government, the SIT and the CBI, to collate details of cases in which investigations have been completed and chargesheets filed, as well as those in which the probe is still underway.

“This information is eminently required for the purpose of determining the strength of the special courts which we propose to establish,” the Bench said.

Expedite probe

The top court also impressed upon the investigating agencies to conclude the pending investigations expeditiously and file the remaining chargesheets. It further directed the Manipur Chief Secretary and the Director General of Police to extend full cooperation to the investigating agencies and ensure effective coordination to facilitate the completion of the probes.

“...We, therefore, lay emphasis on both the agencies to do their best to remove the impediments and complete the investigation. In this regard, we direct the State of Manipur, the Chief Secretary and the Director General of Police to provide full cooperation, coordinate with the investigating agencies, and see what kind of assistance can be provided to the CBI/SITs to overcome the challenges highlighted above,” the Bench said.

In August 2023, the top court directed the CBI to take over the investigation of 30 heinous cases and shifted their trials to Assam to inspire confidence among victims and witnesses. It also appointed former Maharashtra Director General of Police Dattatraya Padsalgikar to monitor the investigations and trials, and constituted a three-member committee headed by Justice Gita Mittal, former Chief Justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court, to examine issues relating to the rehabilitation and resettlement of victims.

Taking on record the latest status report filed by the CBI, the Bench noted that chargesheets had been filed in 21 cases, while closure reports had been submitted in six cases, three of which had been accepted. The SIT, which is investigating 3,020 cases across eight districts in Manipur, also apprised the Bench that charges had been framed in 31 cases, trials had commenced in 10 cases, and nearly 2,900 witnesses remained to be examined.

Supply chargesheets to victims

On Friday, advocate Vrinda Grover, appearing for the victims in two cases of sexual violence during the ethnic violence, informed the court that the victims’ families remained in the dark about the progress of the investigations and were yet to receive copies of the chargesheets filed by the CBI and the SIT, despite the court’s earlier directions.

Taking note of the grievance, the Bench directed the legal aid counsel representing the victims to approach the offices of the Chief Justices of the Gauhati and Manipur High Courts to obtain copies of the chargesheets.

“We direct the legal aid counsel, the Member Secretary of the State Legal Services Authority, Manipur, and the Gauhati State Legal Services Authority to immediately contact the office of the Chief Justice of the High Court of Manipur as well as the office of the Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court for the supply of chargesheets wherever the same have been filed but are yet to be supplied to the victims’ families or the legal aid counsel. It goes without saying that the authorities will ensure the supply of the chargesheets as early as possible, and no later than one week from the date the legal aid counsel contacts them,” the Bench ordered.

The Bench also directed the Manipur High Court to look into cases relating to the 30 persons who have remained missing since the outbreak of the ethnic violence.

It further directed the investigating agencies to file fresh status reports before the next date of hearing.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: NTA terminates 47 officials as part of complete overhaul
World.content:
The government and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held talks on Friday (July 24, 2026) at the Constitution Club of India after the Centre “agreed” to the CJP’s demand that the meeting be held at a neutral venue.

The CJP has said the “strictest action” the government could take against examination irregularities was to remove Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement that a Bill providing for stringent action against paper leaks would be introduced in Parliament.

Also Read: PM reaches out to students; Sonam Wangchuk ends fast

The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is “verifying media reports” on the use of pellet guns by the Rapid Action Force (RAF) against unarmed protesters during July 20 march to Parliament in New Delhi, an official said on Friday (July 24, 2026). This comes three days after The Hindu reported the first known instance of security forces using pellet guns on civilians in the national capital.

Also Read: Student protests are the consequence of Modi government’s policies, writes Sonia Gandhi

Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his indefinite hunger strike after the government assured him that his demands would be met. He announced the end of his fast after Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at the Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around Thursday (July 23, 2026) midnight and conveyed the government’s assurances.

World.title: Holiday for schools, PU colleges in DK, Udupi on July 25
World.content: Dakshina Kannada and Udupi district administrations have declared a holiday for all schools and pre-university colleges in the twin districts on Saturday in view of an orange alert. The holiday is also applicable to all anganwadis, Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and polytechnics offering diploma courses.

World.title: Mega PTM 4.0 draws over 7.1 million participants across Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
Samagra Shiksha State Project Director B. Srinivasa Rao on Friday said the Mega Parent-Teacher Meeting (Mega PTM) 4.0 was conducted on a grand scale in government, aided and Model Schools across Andhra Pradesh.

In a statement, he said the programme received an overwhelming response from students, parents, teachers and the community. According to official data compiled till 6 p.m. on Friday, 7,113,536 participants, including students, parents, teachers, donors, public representatives, alumni and other stakeholders, took part in the event.

Mr. Rao said 43,410 of the 44,076 schools in the State, accounting for 98.42%, successfully conducted the programme. Reports from the remaining 666 schools were awaited.

He expressed gratitude, on behalf of the Department of School Education and Samagra Shiksha, to the officials, students, parents, teachers, public representatives, donors, alumni and all others who contributed to the success of Mega PTM 4.0.

World.title: 15 security personnel killed, 12 militants dead in attack on checkpoint in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
World.content:
The military said the attackers first attempted to storm the checkpoint but were forced back by security personnel. (Representational/Generated using AI)

A suicide bomber backed by armed militants attacked a security checkpoint in Pakistan’s northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, killing 15 security personnel, the military said on Friday.

According to the military, the overnight attack took place in the Tank district, where security forces successfully repelled the initial assault and killed 12 militants during the operation.

The military said the attackers first attempted to storm the checkpoint but were forced back by security personnel. The militants then rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the perimeter wall of the facility, causing a powerful explosion that inflicted extensive damage on the checkpoint.

Those killed in the attack included 12 soldiers, two police officers and a former forest department official, the military said.

World.title: Cargo ship hit in Russian strikes in Black Sea was carrying grain: India
World.content:
In response to Moscow indicating that a ship in Black Sea — in which four Indians were killed — was targeted for carrying military supplies for Ukraine, India said that the vessel was carrying “grain” as cargo.

This is significant with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar raising the issue of targeting of ships and killing of Indian seafarers with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, and Delhi summoning a senior Russian diplomat in the Capital to lodge an official protest.



The Kremlin had earlier defended the missile strike on the cargo ship, saying Russian forces will continue targeting vessels it believes are carrying military supplies for Ukraine.

World.title: LeBron James set to join Philadelphia 76ers after leaving Los Angeles Lakers
World.content:
Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James goes to the basket in the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Cleveland Cavaliers in Cleveland. (AP Photo)

Legendary basketball player LeBron James on Friday announced that he will be joining the Philadelphia 76ers for his record breaking 24th NBA season, ending an eight year association with the Los Angeles Lakers, a team he lead to a title in 2020 after two separate stints with the Cleveland Cavaliers and four years with the Miami Heat.

“This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. ⁠I still ​want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship,” James wrote on social media. “I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always be home!”

World.title: ‘You are the ugliest woman’: Apara Mehta reveals why she and Darshan Jariwala separated
World.content:
Veteran television actor Apara Mehta, fondly remembered for playing Savita Mansukh Virani in Ekta Kapoor’s iconic television serial Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, recently opened up about her marriage with actor Darshan Jariwala. During an interview, she revealed why the couple has been living separately for over two decades and recalled the conversation that changed their relationship forever.

In a conversation with Hauterrfly, Apara Mehta recalled receiving an unexpected call from Darshan Jariwala while she was in the United States. “I was in the USA. It was our wedding anniversary, and I called him from there. He said, ‘We really need to talk.’ I thought, ‘What does he want to talk about?'”

She said that after returning to India, Darshan told her he wanted to end their marriage. “So I came back from the USA after doing my shows. I landed at 3 o’clock, reached home by 5, and I had a 7 o’clock shift in the morning. And he just said, ‘You know, Apara, we need to separate because I’ve fallen out of love with you. I do not like you anymore, and you are the ugliest woman I’ve come across in my life.'”

Also Read | Lathis in Delhi, heroes on screen: As Singham turns 15, Bollywood’s supercop myth shattered

‘The doors are always open for him’

Recalling how she processed the conversation, Apara Mehta said, “He was sitting on the swing with a cup of tea in the morning, and I simply left for my shoot. I had three major scenes to film that day. I had returned from the USA at 5 in the morning, so in between takes I kept dozing off. Later that afternoon, when I was fully conscious again, I thought, ‘What did Darshan just say? He couldn’t have meant it.'”

She further revealed that Darshan Jariwala eventually moved out of their home, but their relationship has remained cordial over the years. “And then, one day, he just left home. It is still our home. He has gone. The doors are always open. He can come back. But I also know that he might not. I’m telling you, he’ll never find anybody like me, and I’ll never find anybody like him. And yes, living separately, we are so comfortable with each other. We can still complete each other’s sentences.”

Darshan Jariwala is known for his performances in films such as Gandhi, My Father, Guru, and Ajab Prem Ki Ghazab Kahani, among others. He married Apara Mehta in 1982, and the couple has a daughter. Although they have been living separately since 2003, they have never legally divorced.

World.title: Pimpri-Chinchwad: Citizens living along Pavana, Indrayani riverbanks urged to stay alert as water level rises
World.content:
All necessary machinery and systems were kept on high alert to handle emergency situations arising from rains. (Source: Express Photo)

Even as water levels in the three rivers flowing through Pimpri Chinchwad rose due to the discharge of water from the dams, the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) appealed to citizens residing on riverbank areas to remain alert.

All necessary machinery and systems were kept on high alert to handle emergency situations arising from rains.

Continuous rains lashed Pimpri-Chinchwad city for several hours on Friday, increasing levels of the Pavana, Mula, and Indrayani rivers, accompanied by water discharged from the dams.

The Pavana Dam is was approximately 97% full till Friday evening. With rains in its catchment area, water was discharged into the riverbed to regulate the dam’s storage. At 8:00 pm the same day, approximately 7,000 cusecs of water was discharged from the dam into the Pavana riverbed, officials said.

World.title: Anita Advani recalls Rajesh Khanna’s reunion with Anju Mahendru: ‘They would laugh’
World.content:
When Rajesh Khanna and Dimple Kapadia separated, it was Anita Advani who became the actor’s closest companion. She lived with him at his iconic bungalow, Aashirwad, for over a decade until his death in 2012. Claiming she had known Rajesh even before his 1973 marriage to Dimple, Anita often described herself as his “surrogate wife”, saying she managed both his household and his personal life. But before Anita and Dimple—there was Anju Mahendru, Rajesh Khanna’s longtime girlfriend. During their relationship, Anju was a constant presence in his life and even managed his home. Although the couple parted ways bitterly after Rajesh married Dimple, they reconciled years later following his separation. In the actor’s final years, Anju frequently visited him and looked after him as his health deteriorated. Interestingly, Anita insists Anju’s return never caused friction between them.



Recalling how Rajesh and Anju rekindled their friendship, Anita said on the Meri Saheli podcast that it all began during a trip to Sharjah for a cricket tournament. “We had gone to Sharjah for the matches when Anju and Rajesh met and spoke. I’m not entirely sure, but I think that’s when their friendship was rekindled. During those matches, all the film personalities would sit together in the VIP boxes.”

She added that their warmth towards each other was unmistakable. “I would often slip away to shop. Sometimes Anju would be there, sometimes she wouldn’t be. Whenever they met, they would smile and laugh. After all, they had shared a very deep relationship. Some bonds never completely disappear.”



When asked whether Anju Mahendru’s return made her feel insecure, Anita dismissed the idea. “Anju and I were always cordial. There was never any jealousy between us. We greeted each other with love and respect. Even today, we meet.”

ALSO READ | Rajesh Khanna bought star’s ‘lucky’ home; was furious when Salman Khan bid for his Aashirwad

In an earlier interview with Meri Saheli, Anita Advani made another startling claim—that she and Rajesh Khanna had secretly married.

“We got married privately, but in the film industry nobody talks openly about such things. People say they’re friends or in a relationship. It was already known in the media that I was with him, so neither of us felt the need to publicly announce our marriage.”

According to Anita Advani, the ceremony took place inside Aashirwad. “We had a small temple at home. I had a mangalsutra made with gold and black beads. He made me wear it. Then he applied sindoor and said, ‘From today, you are my responsibility.’ That’s how we got married one night.”



Despite claiming to have shared her life with Rajesh Khanna for years, Anita said she was not allowed to attend his funeral after his death in 2012. “They had stationed bouncers outside to stop me from entering. Friends warned me that I wouldn’t be allowed inside. Some even suggested I carry a camera and record everything, but I couldn’t do that on such a solemn day. Instead, I stayed away and performed my own chautha for him alone at a temple.”

Long before Anita Advani entered his life, Rajesh Khanna’s romance with Anju Mahendru had been one of Bollywood’s most talked-about relationships. The two dated for several years before their relationship ended amid reports of Rajesh’s possessiveness and growing insecurities. Their breakup became the subject of industry lore after Rajesh reportedly chose to take his wedding procession to Dimple Kapadia past Anju’s residence—a gesture widely interpreted as a dramatic and public statement marking the end of their relationship.
