How do officers demonstrate accountability? How has violence and cruelty become so deeply rooted among 18- to 20-year-olds that it repeatedly leads to deaths? What is the army doing to foster mutual respect, discipline and responsibility?

What is especially alarming is that intolerance and aggression are becoming increasingly visible in society. And yes, much of the responsibility lies with the country’s top leadership, which speaks to society in a language that fuels division, hostility and hatred. That atmosphere eventually seeps into people’s everyday relationships.

We must overcome this nightmare. Let us each begin with the people around us.”

Death of soldier in the Armenian Armed Forces

World.title: Tens of thousands flee fires in France, blazes merge outside Madrid
World.content:
Tens of thousands of people have fled wildfires in southwest France by car and boat and Spain declared a national emergency as huge blazes merged outside Madrid and searing heat left tinder-dry conditions across Europe.

French authorities ordered the total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula, a tourism hotspot on the Atlantic Coast. Two fires merged outside Madrid, and a third was on the verge of joining them, government officials said.

"I had to run from my house. There was a ball of fire. If I'd taken five more minutes, it would have wiped us out," evacuee Enrique Martin said in a shelter in Cebreros, west of Madrid.

Fires burn across the Cap Ferret Peninsula in the south of France. (Reuters :Stephane Mahe)

Both France and Spain sought help from the European Union as the blazes strained firefighting and other emergency services. The national emergency - the first ever issued over a wildfire in Spain - opened up federal funding to tackle the crisis.

"This is the worst wildfire in our region's history," Madrid's regional leader Isabel Diaz Ayuso said after telling reporters the fires had merged.

" It's the perfect storm of very high temperatures and ceaseless winds that aren't letting up. "

In southwest France, authorities sent boats to help the evacuation and a total of about 63,000 people, many of them tourists, were told to get out as two major, separate fires threatened homes and campsites, officials said.

"From our home, we had a view of the fires ... We could see the clouds becoming darker and darker," said Yoan Urien, who left late on Thursday after police told everyone in his neighbourhood in the town of Biscarrosse to leave.

"I was able to find somewhere to take shelter with my pets, but ... it's quite a shock," the 26-year-old said.

France's emergency response resources have been exhausted during the summer heatwave. (AP Photo: Caroline Blumberg)

The other major fire, which began in nearby Saumos, north of Cap Ferret, is threatening to cut off the only road out of the peninsula and is the largest so far this season in France, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told local television.

It has torn through more than 10,000 hectares (24,700 acres) of forest and burned 80 homes, completely destroying about 50 of them, he said.

"It breaks my heart. Because it's such a pleasant place to live, seeing it go up in smoke is truly sad," said family caregiver Corinne Paillaube.

"It's totally apocalyptic," said Ambre Dubos, from the nearby Landes region.

Devastating fire season

In Spain, more than 19,000 people were ordered to evacuate from towns in the mountains west of Madrid, as more than 2,000 personnel and 10 aircraft struggled in vain to prevent the fires converging, Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said.

A short time later another 7,000 people were told to leave from two new localities west of Madrid that were under threat by wildfires.

A third fire in Avila province was on the verge or may have already merged with the two in Madrid, Nicanor Sen, the government representative for the Castile and Leon region, told reporters.

"It is very bad news," Nicanor Sen Velez said.

Fires near Madrid are feared to be the worst in the country's history. (AP Photo: Manu Fernandez)

The area west of Madrid, where many residents from the capital have second homes, is densely populated. In just one development 43 homes had been destroyed, Diaz Ayuso said.

That played a role in the government decision to declare a national emergency, Grande-Marlaska said.

It is the second consecutive year that Spain has faced a particularly destructive fire season.

More than 29 major fires have broken out in Spain so far this year, damaging a surface area five times greater than at the same stage in 2025, when a record area was destroyed, Environment Minister Sara Aagesen said in a social media post.

Spanish police said a man had been arrested and another person was under investigation for allegedly setting off a vast fire in the Madrid region by using a farm vehicle despite a ban in the tinderbox conditions.

Heat hits crops, nuclear plant cooling

Wildfires have burnt more land in Europe already this year than the annual average in the past two decades, data shows as the world's fastest-warming continent has endured three stifling, virtually back-to-back heatwaves so far this year.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is increasing the intensity of heatwaves, droughts and wildfires, while also creating conditions for sudden, destructive storms.

Greece was sending two CL-415 firefighting aircraft to Madrid and will operate across the area of Toledo, the Greek civil protection ministry said.

More than 30,000 people have been evacuated from parts of France due to ongoing fires. (Reuters: Stephane Mahe)

Croatia said it sent on Friday a Canadair CL-415 firefighting aircraft with two crews and 11 Croatian army technical staff to help France battle fires.

After a short reprieve over the weekend, average temperatures in France are expected to rise sharply again next week, according to official weather forecaster Meteo France. The high temperatures are expected to warm French rivers that are used to cool nuclear reactors and could lead to further restrictions, as the reactors reduce output to comply with environmental protection measures.The Golfech 2 nuclear reactor in southern France has remained offline since July 7 due to heat-related restrictions, operator EDF's data showed.

Weeks of hot weather are also taking a toll on the condition of the maize crop in France.

World.title: US and Iran trade strikes after Trump vows 'major military punishment'
World.content:
US missiles have struck targets across Iran, reaching as far as the Caspian coast, as Iran hits US bases across the region and warns of more strikes.

It comes after President Donald Trump vowed "major military punishment" for Tehran and its Houthi allies in Yemen over moves to block a second major international shipping route.

Two weeks after the collapse of an interim truce meant to end the war, Iranian armed forces have responded by firing at US bases in neighbouring countries and warning people there that they may strike non-military buildings used by US personnel.

The Iranian army said Mr Trump's threats only strengthened its resolve, claiming to have attacked US military equipment depots at Al-Adiri, latterly named Camp Buehring, in northern Kuwait, and the positions of US troops at Camp Arifjan and at Camp Doha, near Kuwait City.

Iran warns people to 'move away' from areas used by the US military

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had also significantly damaged a surveillance tower used by the US in Bahrain.

While Jordan's military said it had intercepted seven missiles and six drones launched by Iran on Friday.

The military said the interceptions, performed by air defence systems and air force planes, "resulted in no casualties or material damage".

The US Central Command says it has carried out strikes on Iranian military targets. (US Central Command)

In exchange, US missiles struck a Revolutionary Guards Navy headquarters in the Ziba Kenar area of the Caspian Sea province of Gilan while also hitting Piranshahr, in West Azerbaijan Province, near Iran's border with Iraq, according to state media.

Four people were killed and five injured in a US missile attack on the Iranian city of Ahvaz, state broadcaster IRIB said.

In a statement read out by Iran's state media, the Revolutionary Guards warned the public in the Gulf countries of potential strikes against US military personnel who may be using "buildings in cities as locations to direct their crimes".

It told people to "immediately move away from areas within a 500 metre radius of covert and hidden locations used by US military personnel".

Red Sea blockade pushes up oil prices

A Yemeni government army officer in Bab el-Mandeb, Yemen, earlier in the war. (Reuters)

The fighting comes after the Houthis, who control northern and western Yemen, said this week they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, which has diverted millions of barrels of oil each day by pipeline to the Red Sea to skirt Iran's near-total blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

The blockade has stoked global inflation and fanned fears of an economic downturn.

Houthis declare maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia In a statement, the Houthis' military spokesperson Yahya Saree says the group will enforce the blockade against its "criminal Saudi enemy", effective immediately.

Houthi fighters struck two Saudi tankers on Thursday in the Red Sea's Bab el-Mandeb strait, pushing oil prices 7 per cent higher to pierce the $100 ($143) per barrel level for the first time since May but fell back under $100 on Friday.

Mr Trump wrote on social media he would hold Iran accountable for any further attacks by the fighters "and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves".

He also said that any damage to cargo ships would be paid for with Iranian money, referring to frozen Iranian assets held by the United States, but without specifying how.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi responded with a warning on X, saying no one's assets were safe once governments normalised such confiscation.

"Ensuing chaos will not be pretty or peaceful," he wrote.

Reuters

World.title: Singer Chris Brown pleads guilty to affray over London nightclub incident
World.content:
US singer Chris Brown has pleaded guilty to a charge of affray over what prosecutors described as a bottle attack on a producer in a London nightclub three years ago, with more serious assault charges dropped.

Brown, 37, and his vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, 40, stood in the dock at London's Southwark Crown Court and spoke only to confirm their names and their guilty pleas over the incident at London's Tape nightclub in February 2023.

The pair had been charged with attempting to inflict grievous bodily harm and a less serious charge of assault causing actual bodily harm to Abraham Diaw, which the pair had denied and were due to go to trial in October.

Co-defendant rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who performs under the name Hoody Baby also pleaded guilty to affray. (Reuters: Jaimi Joy)

Brown and Akinlolu pleaded guilty to the charge of affray, admitting they "used or threatened unlawful violence towards another and their conduct taken together was such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness ... to fear for their personal safety".

Prosecutor Heidi Stonecliffe said the other charges would not proceed to trial and Brown and Akinlolu were granted bail ahead of their sentencing at the same court on October 26.

The maximum sentence for affray is three years' imprisonment and Judge Tony Baumgartner said that "all options" would be open to the court.

Claire Campbell from the Crown Prosecution Service said in a statement: "This was a vicious and unprovoked attack by Brown and Akinlolu in a crowded nightclub where Brown used a glass bottle as a weapon to strike the victim's head twice.

"This kind of violence is entirely unacceptable, and the Crown Prosecution Service will work tirelessly – with the police and partners across the criminal justice system – to pursue cases like this, and prove that no one is above the law."

Prosecutors had alleged Brown launched an "unprovoked attack" on Diaw with a tequila bottle, with Akinlolu and Brown said to have continued to attack Diaw as he tried to flee.

He was arrested in May 2025 having returned to Britain for the first time since the incident and initially denied bail, throwing his worldwide "Breezy Bowl XX" tour into doubt.

But Brown was eventually released after promising to pay a £5 million ($6.66 million) security fee, allowing the tour to go ahead.

The singer left court to cheers from fans chanting "Breezy! Breezy!" before signing autographs and then getting into a waiting car.

World.title: Russian missile strike kills 10 at Ukraine defence industry event
World.content:
A Russian ballistic missile strike has killed 10 people and injured almost 100 others at a defence industry event in Ukraine's Kyiv region, Ukrainian officials say.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that efforts to determine what happened were underway but did not identify the exact target.

"A rescue operation is currently underway in the Kyiv region following a Russian missile strike," he said on Telegram.

The Ukrainian Council of Defence Industry said the missile strike hit a site where representatives were present. (Reuters Photo: State Emergency Service of Ukraine)

Kyiv region acting governor, Ruslan Oliynyk, said preliminary information indicated the missile strike hit a private training ground where events were taking place.

The Ukrainian Council of Defence Industry said that representatives of Ukraine's defence industry were at the site when it was hit, but that it had not organised the event and participants' exact location had not been made public.

Valerii Borovyk, founder of Ukrainian drone company First Contact, told Ukrainian media that a missile struck a training ground where a defence industry exhibition was being held.

Ukraine's prosecutor-general, Ruslan Kravchenko, said that a criminal investigation had been launched into whether officials improperly carried out their duties in organising and conducting the event.

Kremlin says it will pursue 'total victory'

The strike came as the Kremlin said it believed US President Donald Trump was sincere in efforts to end the Ukraine war but would continue fighting while waiting for Washington to present new peace proposals.

"Yes, (fighting) is not the preferred path, but given the absence of prospects for peace, we will see it through to the end, to total victory," Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state television.

"We will wait for new (US) proposals."

Dmitry Peskov says Moscow will pursue its military objectives in Ukraine while waiting for new US peace proposals. (Sputnik: Gavriil Grigorov/Pool via Reuters)

Mr Peskov said Russia had accepted a previous US proposal, but claimed it had been rejected by Ukraine.

"The Americans — President Trump, his negotiators — are sincere in their desire to formulate options acceptable to everyone," he said.

"The Americans could not persuade the Ukrainians … who were being incited by the Europeans."

Zelenskyy just scored an 'own goal' The Ukrainian president's decision to fire his popular, tech-savvy 35-year-old Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov last week baffled many. Analysts say what happens next could be pivotal to the war.

The last three-way peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US took place in February, shortly before the US and Israel went to war with Iran.

The Kremlin has repeatedly said it hopes US-led mediation will resume once the Middle East crisis has eased.

The top US and Russian diplomats met briefly in Asia this week. Russia has been saying for weeks that it is ready to host Mr Trump's envoys for talks in Moscow, but no date has been announced.

Mr Peskov said Washington's position was ambiguous because it was "continuing to pump Ukraine full of weaponry" while talking about wanting to end the war.

"However, we must leverage this duality in the Trump administration's position wherever it aligns with our interests," he said.

"And their desire to facilitate a peaceful settlement is entirely in line with our interests."

ABC/Wires

World.title: Bali bans two Dutch men alleged to have hosted discriminatory run club
World.content:
Bali's Immigration department has banned two Dutch men from Indonesia for organising a run club event 'fraught with discrimination against local residents'.

It comes after online complaints by Indonesians about the 'Entourage Bali' community went viral.

The organisers of the event have been banend from Indonesia and placed on a travel ban list. (Instagram: @entourage.bali)

In a statement, Bali's Director General of Immigration, Hendarsam Marantoko, said he condemned the event, and that immigration would impose an entry ban on the 'two foreign nationals involved'.

"The Bali Silent Disco running event organised by foreign nationals (is) suspected of violating regulations and being fraught with discrimination against local residents."

" This running event represents a state within a state, "

"I have instructed the Bali immigration team to inspect the event organiser, if any foreign nationals are involved, arrest them immediately."

Immigration officials say the two Dutch men, identified as JAS, 35, and HQV, 37, left Bali for Singapore on Wednesday night.

Officials say they've been slapped with an entry ban and placed on the travel ban list.

"Foreigners must not act as though they can establish their own rules and exclusivity within the jurisdiction of Indonesia," the statement reads.

Immigration officials said foreign nationals were not allowed to manage an event in Indonesia, or act as event organisers.

Alleged bias to western names

A social media post of an Entourage Bali event in May shows a large group of people running through the streets of Canggu, wearing headphones and waving their hands in the air.

On social media, one Indonesian woman said that when she messaged 'Entourage Bali' to join the community, she received a message that her application would be reviewed, while her husband's application with a 'western name and number' was accepted immediately.

The organisers said incorrect automated responses had been sent to some hopeful participants. (Threads: @channisaraa)

In a post on social media, Balinese based Indonesian Senator Niluh Djelantik said "our hospitality should never be mistaken for a license to disrespect us."

On Friday she said she had spoken with immigration officials.

"Utilising public spaces while rejecting local residents is unacceptable," she said.

Senator Niluh Djelantik said the apparent rejection of locals was unacceptable. (ABC News: Tim Swanston)

Run club responds

In a statement posted on its social media pages, Entourage Bali said "we are extremely sorry for the people that have been offended and hurt, and we have never meant to be disrespectful or discriminating to anyone".

"Entourage was created as a community for digital nomads in Bali to help people who are new to the island connect with others and do fun activities together during their stay … our community includes members from many countries, including Indonesia."

Entourage Bali said that Indonesians made up "the largest group of participants" in the silent disco run, "representing representing nearly 25% of all tickets sold."

"However, we have made errors in the automated approval process for our WhatsApp groups,

" While we were trying to create a place where digital nomads could meet, a bias was created that some (and not all) +62 numbers / Indonesians were incorrectly rejected. "

"We are pausing all our events and activities for now. We take full accountability for what has happened and promise we will make real changes going forward."

The organisers said 25 per cent of ticket holders were indonesian. (Instagram: @entourage.bali)

The ABC has contacted Entourage Bali for comment.

Visa understanding urged

This blacklisting comes as Bali immigration cracks down on foreign nationals working while on a tourist visa.

On the Australian Smartraveller website it urges Australians to "understand your visa conditions".

“It's illegal to work, conduct research or volunteer if you're on a tourist visa. This includes creating or posting online content for payment or commercial purposes."

"Indonesian authorities may consider it a breach of visa conditions if you create content for commercial purposes while you're on a tourist visa, even if the content is published after you've departed Indonesia."

World.title: Police intercept car with 'significant' bomb near Northern Ireland border
World.content:
Police in Ireland have found an "extremely significant" bomb inside a vehicle close to the border with Northern Ireland.

Police said detectives requested the assistance of the army's Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team after they stopped the vehicle on Wednesday.

On Friday, police said the EOD team had completed an examination of the vehicle but would not release the outcome "for operational reasons".

"What we found was an extremely significant seizure," Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly said.

"This was an explosive device."

The driver of the vehicle, a woman in her 20s, was arrested and continues to be detained on suspicion of offences against the state.

A man in his 40s has also been arrested in connection with the investigation.

The vehicle was stopped close to the County Monaghan town of Carrickmacross, which is about 10 kilometres from the open border between the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland.

Sporadic attacks by militant groups, often attempted car bombings, continue in Northern Ireland almost three decades since a peace deal largely ended sectarian violence in the British-run region.

There have been two car bomb incidents this year in Northern Ireland that police have blamed on dissident republicans, including one that exploded outside a police station on the outskirts of Belfast in April.

The incidents reflect the decades of violence known as the Troubles which killed almost 3,600 people before the 1998 Good Friday peace accord.

"We certainly know that there are a small minority of dissident republicans who did not agree with the Good Friday Agreement, they did not put weapons and explosives (out of use)," Commissioner Kelly said.

"There's a small minority of these individuals, I would describe them as radicalised republicans, and this is a threat that we're going to continue to face for some time."

World.title: What it feels like to have your sport dumped from the Commonwealth Games
World.content:
As the Commonwealth Games kicked off on its first full day of competition, plenty more sat at at home, many wishing it could be them.

Organisers in 2026 ditched badminton, hockey, wrestling, road cycling, mountain biking, rhythmic gymnastics, rugby sevens, squash, table tennis, triathlon, beach volleyball, cricket and, the most storied of all, diving.

It has been held at every edition since the first Empire Games in 1930, until this year.

Of the 22 Commonwealth Games diving events, Anabelle Smith went to the past four, including Glasgow 2014.

Twelve years ago she won bronze in the women's synchronised 3m springboard with Maddison Keeney, but not in Glasgow like the rest of her team.

This dive for Smith (left) and Keeney was at Glasgow 2014 in name only. (Getty Images: Quinn Rooney)

The Scottish capital did not have a facility to allow for diving, so Smith, Keeney and Co were shipped to Edinburgh, the site of the 1970 and 1986 Games.

"[There was] obvious disappointment from the divers … but also an understanding," Smith told ABC Sport.

"It made sense they weren't just gonna ship the divers up to Edinburgh, disappointing but they'll power on and look ahead now."

The 33-year-old had not been planning to defend her 3m synchro gold medal from Birmingham 2022, but is instead attending her fifth Games as a spectator and part of the Australian team's connection and belonging squad.

How we got to Glasgow 2026 The bumpy road to Glasgow 2026 has produced a Commonwealth Games that will look a little different than the ones that came before.

She's joined by other athletes who have seen their sports axed, including beach volleyballer Chris McHugh and Melissa 'Milly' Tapper.

Her sport of table tennis was also axed after being included in six straight Games from 2002 to 2022.

Tapper, an Olympian and Paralympian, embodies the inclusive and integrated nature of the Games perhaps better than anyone.

She won team bronze at Glasgow 2014 and singles gold on home soil on the Gold Coast in 2018, and is still getting the chance to flash her skills in the team lounge at the decked-out Glasgow Argyle Hotel.

Loading Instagram content

"I've got a little bit of a call-up having the table tennis table in there," she said.

"We've had plenty of athletes and even some staff come through and challenge. Being around athletes everyone's competitive. It's a lot of fun.

"So even though table tennis isn't technically in the Games, it's still a part of the Games."

Table tennis was a "core sport" for the Commonwealth Games and falls into the category of many of the 2026 events, in that it could be held in existing halls.

Melissa Tapper has represented Australia at the Olympics, Paralympics and Commonwealth Games. (Getty Images: Matt Roberts)

Field hockey, however, requires a bit more space and bespoke facilities. Its history in the Commonwealth Games is not quite as long as diving's, but it had an elevated status as a "core sport".

In 2014, it was held at the Glasgow National Hockey Centre, which remains operational and is located along the River Clyde, within the 13-kilometre corridor of the pared-back 2026 Games.

When cuts were being made for 2026, the International Hockey Federation (FIH) and Commonwealth member nations lobbied for the sport's inclusion, but they missed out as organisers opted largely for indoor sports with athletics the only outdoor event.

Glasgow 2026 events 3x3 basketball/wheelchair basketball

Artistic gymnastics

Athletics

Bowls

Boxing

Judo

Netball

Para powerlifting and weightlifting

Swimming

Track cycling

The Kookaburras have won all seven men's gold medals since 1998, while the Hockeyroos have also never missed the podium, boasting four gold, two silver and a bronze.

Kookaburras captain Eddie Ockenden carried the flag in the Birmingham 2022 opening ceremony, as evidence of the sport's standing in Australia's Commonwealth Games movement, so Hockey Australia was "naturally disappointed" to miss out in 2026.

"Our national teams only play a finite number of international tournaments, making every opportunity to compete in one incredibly valuable," high performance director Bernard Savage said.

"The Commonwealth Games have always been one of those opportunities that our teams have genuinely looked forward to. Beyond the competition itself, the Commonwealth Games provide a unique multi-sport environment that our athletes look forward to and aspire to be a part of.

"The broader interest in the Games has provided an opportunity for our athletes and teams to inspire the next generation of hockey players across Australia and the Commonwealth.

"While this has been disappointing news, our focus remains firmly on our preparation for the 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup."

The World Cup will be played in Belgium and The Netherlands from August 15-30, shortly after the end of the Glasgow Games.

World.title: New report reveals what triggered SA's catastrophic algal bloom crisis
World.content:
After more than 18 months of uncertainty surrounding South Australia's most catastrophic algal bloom crisis, a long-awaited report has been released by the SA government shedding light on the environmental conditions that fuelled the marine event.

The report has concluded that floodwater, a coastal upwelling and a marine heatwave all contributed to the conditions that led to the devastating event, but that there was no "single trigger".

The preliminary investigation was conducted by the South Australian Research and Development Institute (SARDI) into potential drivers of the bloom, and its release was foreshadowed in February, when authorities blamed the bloom on a "convergence" of events — including comments on the nutrient load from River Murray flooding as one of the main factors.

A full report was released today following what the SA government described as an independent peer-review process.

The algal bloom was first detected in March 2025, and is characterised by foamy and discoloured water. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

Report released late

But the date on the report dated back to May 15 this year, which has been questioned by some, including Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young, who slammed the state government for not being up-front on the matter from the beginning.

"We know from the beginning they [SA government] were too slow to act and asleep at the wheel," she said.

" The South Australian government has tried to downplay the impact of the toxic algal bloom on South Australians and on our environment, so I am unsurprised that a peer reviewed report has been sitting on the desk for months. "

Sarah Hanson-Young says the SA government has downplayed the impact of the toxic algal bloom. (ABC News: Craig Hansen)

When asked why the report was made public late, South Australia's Primary Industries Minister Clare Scriven said it needed to go through the processes, including being peer-reviewed.

"It needed to go to the Algal Bloom Taskforce, and be analysed by my office and the taskforce," Ms Scriven said.

"It was reviewed by independent reviewers from Tasmania and the United States."

But ecologist Faith Coleman, who resigned from SA HAB (Harmful Algal Bloom) Scientific Advisory Committee and SA Algae Bloom Reference Group earlier this year, said the report did not need to be peer reviewed and should not have taken that long.

"It shouldn't have needed to gone off and spend all the time from April to now being peer-reviewed, that is a lot of months," she said.

But she welcomed the transparency from the government saying the findings will be useful going forward.

Faith Coleman has asked the state government to release more data. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

The findings

The report found that there were three major contributing factors that triggered the ideal conditions for the bloom to develop, including floodwater, a coastal upwelling and a marine heatwave.

It was found that the bloom developed and intensified during an unprecedented marine heatwave.

The report stated that while temperature alone may not explain bloom initiation, the associated calm conditions, reduced wind mixing and enhanced water-column stratification were considered a key enabling factor, favouring motile dinoflagellates such as Karenia.

It said that multi-decadal analyses show that the bloom developed following a period of prolonged environmental pre-conditioning.

SARDI's executive director Professor Mike Steer said a comprehensive amount of research had gone into finding these out.

"There's not a single smoking gun, there wasn't one particular environmental factor that was the culprit for this algal bloom, in fact it was a convergence of many different things," Professor Steer said.

"This is really important information to understand because if we're going to develop a forecasting index for harmful algal blooms for SA or Australia in the future then we really need to understand these fundamental drivers."

Mike Steer says there are notable gaps in the data collected. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

He admitted there were still gaps in the data they have collected and analysed.

"Now there are notably gaps in those data, but we'll seek to fill them as we go forward," he said.

But Professor Steer said he was surprised how quickly the team was able to pull together the report.

"I thought it was going to take us a lot longer to get where we are at, but the foundation that we have set is really promising," he said.

Ms Scriven said while nothing could be done to stop the algal bloom from occurring, the research helps to be more prepared.

Clare Scriven says nothing can be done to prevent a harmful algal bloom from occurring. (ABC News: Trent Murphy)

But Ms Coleman has asked the state government to release more data.

"It's not a rigorous review of the science that we would've liked to see at this point," she said.

" It is a good technical report, I'm looking forward to seeing a huge pile of data to go with it, rather than just the dot points. "

"I'd like them to release the data about all of the other hazardous species that have occurred, not just Karenia."

Ms Coleman said she also hopes the government will change conversations around the Murray River — which was persistently blamed as one of the main contributing factors.

"That has been a major issue for us all the way along is the comment that it is the River Murray, because that impacts how we manage the biggest most regulated river in the nation," she said.

There's gap in the data

Professor Steer said there was still a lot that is not known and that it was going to take time to look at some of the knowledge gaps.

The algal bloom devastated South Australia's coastline, resulting in the deaths of significant numbers of marine life. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

"One of the challenges in science is that in answering one particular question you generate ten more," he said.

" There is an incredible complexity of issues that are happened within a marine environment and the complexity within the harmful algal bloom community dynamics is just next level. "

Professor Steer said the report is a strong foundation for the new office to continue their research in collaboration with national and international jurisdictions.

This includes looking at topics such as, "The different biochemicals are produced by the harmful algal bloom species, the role the environment plays in persisting algal blooms, and understanding the impact on key recreational commercial fisheries and marine ecosystems," he said.

Going forward, Professor Steer said the algal bloom crisis and the report will set down precedent on how to deal with similar crisis in the future.

" We don't want the legacy of the bloom, our response to the bloom being our legacy, we want the preparedness for future blooms to be something that we'll work towards. "

"Our focus now is on improving our science and understanding it so we're better prepared in the future."

I’m here at the Armadillo for the para powerlifting, with Aussie Hani Watson competing tonight in Glasgow (morning back in Australia).

If Watson’s name sounds familiar it’s because she’s already made history. The Queenslander broke Australia’s 16-year medal drought in the sport when she won bronze in the women’s heavyweight at Birmingham 2022 with a best lift of 127kg – nearly 30kg more than her body weight.

Watson was born with bilateral metaphyseal dysplasia, which bowed her tibia and femur bones. She has undergone several surgeries as a result, and has previously told media her upper body strength is her “superpower”.

Like other lifting competitions so far, the action will split into two: group B has just started, and Watson will follow in group A.

Stay tuned.

World.title: By milling its own flour, this local bakery doesn’t just make better bread, it builds stronger communities
World.content:
Review Eating outPerth By milling its own flour, this local bakery doesn’t just make better bread, it builds stronger communities Max Veenhuyzen July 25, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

1 / 3 Apricot bear claws are among the seasonal pastries served at Miller + Baker. Miller + Baker 2 / 3 Pastries and sandwiches constantly rotate throughout the year. Miller + Baker 3 / 3 Golden croissants and viennoiserie are a core part of Miller + Baker’s offering. Miller + Baker Previous Slide Next Slide 14 / 20 How we score Miller + Baker Bakery$$$$ Can a bakery be classified as a restaurant? If you define a restaurant as a place where customers can buy something to eat and drink and there’s somewhere for them to sit down and enjoy their purchase, I think so. Which means that Miller + Baker – a Northbridge bakery-cafe with indoor counter seats plus some tables and chairs scattered across the Lake Street footpath – absolutely fits the description.



But what if you decided to open a bakery that became more than somewhere to eat? I’m not sure if that was Rachel and Mark Taylor’s goal when they opened Miller + Baker in the former home of Italian bakery Casa del Dolce back in 2019, but seven years on, the Taylors’ Little-Corner-Bakery-That-Could feels like more than just somewhere to buy bread. Miller + Baker owners Rachel and Mark Taylor. Max Veenhuyzen Restaurant reviews, news and the hottest openings served to your inbox. Sign up Inspired by the sourdough and organic food culture the couple enjoyed while living in Copenhagen, the Taylors returned to Perth and were keen to recreate their experience. One such lesson was the deliciousness and nutritional value of sourdough bread made from good wheat. Fate led the Taylors to the Heggarty family, founders of Natural Intelligence Farming and owners of a wheat farm in Mollerin in the Wheatbelt.



The Heggartys’ regenerative agriculture approach – a system that, in a pesticide-free nutshell, eschews chemical inputs in favour of natural approaches that improve soil health – resonated with what the Taylors were looking for. With wheat (and occasionally rye) supply locked in, they set about learning the finer points of the stone mill they bought from America and began turning this single-origin grain into freshly milled flour: more nutritious and better tasting than commercially sold commodity flours. But hey, don’t take my word for it - take home one of the bakery’s Millers sourdough loaves and taste if for yourself. A hefty rugby ball of a loaf that contains more wholewheat flour than any other core Miller + Baker product, its dense crumb is the colour of milky tea and reveals bold flashes of, well, wheaten richness with each chew. This is not a bread one buys if they need a neutral, flavourless medium. Miller + Baker works with a range of different wheat strains. Miller + Baker It’s also not a big seller. Or at least, according to the Taylors, compared to the bakery’s regular classic sourdough that, due to its reduced wholewheat flour ratio, boasts a crumb with more spring and puffier pockets of air.



You can take away loaves of classic sourdough too, but if you felt like enjoying it in situ, there’s a glass cabinet filled with ace pre-made sandwiches that are dying to meet you. While the sangers are based on combinations that should be familiar to most – roast beef, ham and cheese, chicken and salad – little details in the kitchen ensure what guests are eating is less lunch bar and more café. The chook for the chicken salad number, for instance, is roasted in-house and moistened with a salad dressing packing a healthy jolt of acidity. The result is a flavour that’s closer to an Eastern European potato salad. Served in gaseous baguettes that are more chewy than crisp, the roast beef roll is made with the good stuff that’s been slowly poached on-site until soft and yielding. Kelly Bucksley at Miller + Baker. Miller + Baker



To finish: a sprightly chimichurri sauce that had more to say than most of the lacklustre versions served around town. The top half of the ham and cheese baguette is dabbed at with hot English mustard while the bottom is primed with thick smears of nutty brown butter. Recent sightings of free agent consultant chef Frankie Dawson treading the boards in the Miller + Baker kitchen can only mean good things for the menu. You’ll spy other people of interest in the bakery too. Steven Jackson, a Perth cook that owned St Kilda’s Miss Jackson café, has been managing the kitchen for the past two years while baker Emanuele Vittozzi keeps close watch on the ovens. Between them, they ensure that the pork and fennel sausage roll is chunky in the best possible ways; the croissants are a healthy mix of crisp and that cotton-wool softness; and that the two-pastry pies – shortcrust cases, puff pastry lids – have lift-off. Beyond supporting small producers and quietly raising awareness of good farming and food nutrition, Miller + Baker is building communities in other ways too. The Taylors are partners in cheery Parkside Coffee down the road; they’ve opened another outpost on Hobart Street in North Perth; the cheery staff host a run club; plus the space next to the bakery is now The Mill Room Mercantile, a polished homewares store. It’s amazing what you can achieve by rethinking what a bakery can be. The low-down Atmosphere: the best neighbourhood bakery since sliced (stone-ground, sourdough) bread Go-to dishes: beef and chimichurri baguette, beef and red wine pie, ham and Gruyere croissant Drinks: coffee roasted by Good People Nice Things plus teas, spiced lattes and other cafe favourites Cost: about $40 for two people, excluding drinks and takeaway treats for later Good Food reviews are booked anonymously and paid independently. A restaurant can’t pay for a review or inclusion in the Good Food Guide.

World.title: Netanyahu, Zelensky to meet Trump at White House, attend senator’s funeral
World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaTrump's White House Netanyahu, Zelensky to meet Trump at White House, attend senator’s funeral July 25, 2026 — 2:30am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky are each scheduled to meet with US President Donald Trump next week. Netanyahu will travel to Washington on Monday and will meet with Trump on Tuesday, according to a statement from Netanyahu’s office. Netanyahu will also attend US senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral, his office said. US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House in April 2025. Getty Images The last time Trump and Netanyahu met in Washington was in February, just weeks before they launched a joint war against Iran. Since then, tensions have grown between the longtime allies, including over how to prosecute the war. Israel had opposed Trump’s recent negotiations with Iran, while Trump was upset over Israeli military action in Lebanon, which he saw as a threat to his diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.



Related Article Updated

Middle East at war Trump warns of ‘massive attack’ on Iran, Australians urged to rethink travel plans But with Iran and the United States fighting once again, Israel has also signalled its willingness to rejoin the conflict. In recent days, Israeli officials have said they’re preparing to respond if Iran launches an attack on Israeli soil. Zelensky is also scheduled to meet with Trump on Tuesday, a White House official said. A Ukrainian source said Zelensky was interested in travelling to the United States, but his team was waiting for official confirmation of Trump’s schedule from the White House. The source added that Ukrainians and US officials had been discussing a proposal for an air ceasefire to take to Russian officials, as part of a new round of peace proposals to try to end the war that began in 2022 with Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.



The source said Ukraine had approached Russian President Vladimir Putin in the past with offers of a ceasefire, which had been turned down. However, some officials believe that pressure on Russia’s economy from ongoing Ukrainian drone and missile strikes may soften Putin’s stance. Zelensky spoke on Wednesday with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about the prospects for renewed peace talks with Russia, and said that Ukrainian and US officials could meet in the US in the coming days. Earlier on Friday, right-wing activist and Trump ally Laura Loomer interviewed Zelensky and said he had told her he would likely be in the US next week for a trip that would include a meeting with Trump. Related Article Analysis

US politics Lindsey Graham, the ‘Three Amigos’ and the shifting politics of Israel Loomer, in a post on X, added that Zelensky said he would attend the funeral for Graham, who died earlier this month. A memorial service for the Republican lawmaker will be held on Tuesday in Washington, where Trump will make remarks ahead of a funeral in Graham’s home state of South Carolina on Wednesday.



Graham was a major supporter of Ukraine, travelling there 10 times since the Russian invasion. He pushed for sanctions on Russia as well as US backing for Kyiv. Reuters/AP Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: ‘This is my last decision’: LeBron James heading to 76ers
World.content:
Breaking SportBasketballNBA ‘This is my last decision’: LeBron James heading to 76ers Frank Pingue July 25, 2026 — 2:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

LeBron James announced his decision on Friday (US time) to join the Philadelphia 76ers for his record-extending 24th NBA season with hopes of helping the franchise snap a 43-year championship drought. The league’s all-time leading scorer spent the last eight seasons of his glittering career with the Los Angeles Lakers, leading them to a title in 2020 after two separate stints with the Cleveland Cavaliers and four years with the Miami Heat. Off to Philadelphia: LeBron James. Getty Images “This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship,” James wrote on social media. “I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you, LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always be home!”



James will join a 76ers team that made the 2026 NBA playoffs by securing the seventh seed through a play-in tournament before falling to the eventual champion New York Knicks in the second round. James did not disclose terms of the deal, but ESPN reported that the four-time champion signed a two-year, $US8 million ($11.5 million) contract with a player option. View post on X A number of teams had been pursuing James, with Cleveland, Miami, the Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves all believed to have been interested in the high-profile free agent. The 41-year-old James, who last March surpassed Robert Parish’s record for most career regular-season games played, has continued to perform at an elite level despite his age.



He earned a league-record 22nd consecutive All-Star selection last February during a season in which he averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists over 60 games. His season ended when the Lakers were swept from the second round of the playoffs. Related Article NBA LeBron James is leaving the Lakers. At 41, he plans to play another season “I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn’t ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game. I still truly love this game, and I have more to give,” James said. “The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out.” In a testament to his durability, James and his son Bronny became the first father-son duo to play together in a regular-season NBA game in October 2024, fulfilling what he had long said was one of his remaining basketball goals.



James, a four-time NBA Finals Most Valuable Player, joined the Lakers in 2018. He set the league record for the longest career in NBA history last year when he surpassed Vince Carter’s mark of 22 seasons. Loading He was selected with the first pick in the 2003 NBA Draft by his hometown Cavaliers, where he spent seven seasons before announcing during a live TV special titled The Decision that he was leaving for Miami. The announcement damaged James’ public image and led to many people burning his replica No. 23 jerseys on Cleveland’s streets that night. In Miami, James teamed up with Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh to create an instant powerhouse that won two NBA titles during their four seasons together in South Beach.



Related Article NBA Knicks break their drought and deliver long-awaited sporting glory to New York James returned to Cleveland and in 2016 rallied the team from a 3-1 series deficit in the NBA Finals to stun the Golden State Warriors and make good on his promise to deliver the Cavaliers their first championship. Two years later, James again left his hometown team, where he remains the franchise leader in nearly every major statistical category, to join the Lakers, where for the first time he played in the NBA’s Western Conference. World.title: ‘Of course we can win it’: Defiant Dangerfield backs the Cats to contend again, despite his injury
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘Of course we can win it’: Defiant Dangerfield backs the Cats to contend again, despite his injury Sam McClure Updated July 25, 2026 — 12:13am ,first published 10:44pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Loading

Patrick Dangerfield has revealed he will likely need to take a break in the coming weeks to manage a troublesome adductor injury, as Geelong face a delicate balancing act between preserving their captain and maintaining their finals push. The Cats skipper, who battled through obvious discomfort in Friday night’s statement victory over Melbourne after an incident just before half-time, said he would undergo further medical assessment after feeling the problem worsen during the match. Patrick Dangerfield addresses his teammates at the MCG. AFL Photos “I’ll see the doctor Monday and see where it’s at,” Dangerfield told The Age after the Cats’ 18.9 (117) to 14.13 (97) win. The veteran admitted that, ideally, he would be afforded time to rest the injury, but said Geelong’s injury list and precarious ladder position meant that decision would not be straightforward.



“In an ideal scenario there’d probably be time for rest, but we’ve just had injuries at the wrong time. We’ve just got to find a way,” he said. Editor's pick Updated

AFL 2026 Geelong superstar agrees to a deal for 2027, Pendlebury still undecided Dangerfield insisted the issue was different to the significant groin injuries that interrupted previous seasons and believed he could continue to play without causing further damage, despite increasing discomfort. “It’s an injury I’ve actually never done before. It happened changing direction,” he revealed. It cast the only significant shadow over one of Geelong’s most important victories of the season.



The Cats ended Melbourne’s previously undefeated record at the MCG under Steven King and, in the process, delivered another compelling reminder that they remain firmly in the premiership conversation. With just weeks remaining before finals, the Cats appear to be building towards September in familiar fashion. “We can win it – of course we can win it,” Dangerfield said. “It’s about getting your best football going at the most important time of the year and then riding that wave once you’ve built it. “It started a couple of weeks ago. We haven’t executed it every time, but all you can worry about is the next moment and preparing yourself for the next big part.



“There was a lot riding on tonight. It was pretty cool for us to get it right.” That confidence was built on one devastating quarter that completely transformed the contest. Melbourne dominated the opening term and should have established a commanding advantage. The Demons controlled territory, won the contest around the ball and repeatedly generated forward entries, yet their wastefulness in front of goal proved costly. They could easily have been four or five goals in front but failed to convert their dominance into scoreboard pressure. View post on X Geelong punished them.



Chris Scott’s side produced a ferocious second-quarter burst, slamming on seven goals to two with a combination of ruthless efficiency, clean ball movement and relentless pressure that overwhelmed Melbourne. It was football played at premiership level. The Cats sliced through Melbourne’s defence with speed and precision, punished turnovers and suddenly looked every bit the experienced September side that has made a habit of peaking late in seasons. Emerging key forward Shannon Neale was the biggest beneficiary. Shannon Neale was a standout for the Cats against the in-form Demons. AFL Photos



The athletic spearhead proved far too powerful for Melbourne defender Lukas Cooke, who was playing just his second AFL game, kicking five goals — four of them before half-time — in one of the finest performances of his career. Cooke fought gamely but was handed one of the toughest assignments in football and Neale’s combination of strength, reach and finishing proved too much to contain. Geelong also entered the game with a clear tactical plan for Melbourne captain Max Gawn. Tom Stewart had another standout night for Geelong. AFL Photos Rather than allowing the superstar ruckman to drift behind the play and influence contests with his marking, the Cats used Mark Blicavs to shadow Gawn around the ground after stoppages. Blicavs’ athleticism and discipline denied Gawn the freedom he so often enjoys as an intercepting presence and limited one of Melbourne’s greatest weapons.



The Demons refused to surrender. Defender-turned-forward Harrison Petty threatened to drag his side back into the contest with a career-best display in attack, finishing with four goals in a performance that, at times, evoked memories of club great Garry Lyon. Every time Melbourne threatened to mount a charge, Petty provided another contest and another goal. But Geelong always had the answers. Dangerfield was quick to praise the club’s emerging talent, singling out defender Connor O’Sullivan as one of the brightest young players in the competition. “I think he’s going to be generational,” Dangerfield said. “He’s going to play for another 15 years. World.title: Grant injured as Rabbitohs all but end Storm’s finals hopes
World.content:
Melbourne captain Harry Grant suffered a hamstring injury in a 28-26 loss to South Sydney that leaves the depleted Storm’s NRL finals aspirations hanging by a thread.

Their hopes of a 16th consecutive finals berth now hinge on five consecutive wins to finish the regular season and even that may not be enough.

Loading

Grant is set to miss at least some of the fight for Melbourne’s season, joining big names Cameron Munster, Xavier Coates, Eli Katoa, Tui Kamikamica and Will Warbrick on the pine.

Harry Grant. Getty Images

The Queensland hooker pulled up sore popping a pass up for Trent Loiero just before half-time in Friday’s clash at Accor Stadium.

He limped to the sidelines and threw his headgear to the ground in frustration.

After a torrid week that claimed David Fifita (suspension), Cam Murray (calf) and Tallis Duncan (hamstring), the Rabbitohs lost their own hooker Brandon Smith (calf) to injury.

But the victory was crucial to South Sydney’s own finals hopes, which had been thrown into jeopardy with two losses from their previous four games.

Souths were staring down the possibility of falling out of the top eight to finish the weekend when Tyran Wishart and Nick Meaney crossed in quick succession during the final 15 minutes.

Right centre Meaney scythed over to give the Storm a two-point lead with 10 minutes to play.

But when fullback Sua Fa’alogo, excellent to that point, fumbled Cody Walker’s 40/20 kick into touch, the home side had the chance to strike back.

Recently re-signed halfback Ashton Ward found Campbell Graham with a beautiful cutout pass on the right side to give Souths a two-point lead that they held.

Rabbitohs winger Campbell Graham scores against Melbourne. NRL Photos

Fa’alogo had been essential as Melbourne, down 8-0 after as many minutes, rallied for a 16-8 half-time lead.

World.content:
I’m here at the Armadillo for the para powerlifting, with Aussie Hani Watson competing tonight in Glasgow (morning back in Australia).

If Watson’s name sounds familiar it’s because she’s already made history. The Queenslander broke Australia’s 16-year medal drought in the sport when she won bronze in the women’s heavyweight at Birmingham 2022 with a best lift of 127kg – nearly 30kg more than her body weight.

Watson was born with bilateral metaphyseal dysplasia, which bowed her tibia and femur bones. She has undergone several surgeries as a result, and has previously told media her upper body strength is her “superpower”.

Like other lifting competitions so far, the action will split into two: group B has just started, and Watson will follow in group A.

Stay tuned.

World.title: By milling its own flour, this local bakery doesn’t just make better bread, it builds stronger communities
World.content:
Review Eating outPerth By milling its own flour, this local bakery doesn’t just make better bread, it builds stronger communities Max Veenhuyzen July 25, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

1 / 3 Apricot bear claws are among the seasonal pastries served at Miller + Baker. Miller + Baker 2 / 3 Pastries and sandwiches constantly rotate throughout the year. Miller + Baker 3 / 3 Golden croissants and viennoiserie are a core part of Miller + Baker’s offering. Miller + Baker Previous Slide Next Slide 14 / 20 How we score Miller + Baker Bakery$$$$ Can a bakery be classified as a restaurant? If you define a restaurant as a place where customers can buy something to eat and drink and there’s somewhere for them to sit down and enjoy their purchase, I think so. Which means that Miller + Baker – a Northbridge bakery-cafe with indoor counter seats plus some tables and chairs scattered across the Lake Street footpath – absolutely fits the description.



But what if you decided to open a bakery that became more than somewhere to eat? I’m not sure if that was Rachel and Mark Taylor’s goal when they opened Miller + Baker in the former home of Italian bakery Casa del Dolce back in 2019, but seven years on, the Taylors’ Little-Corner-Bakery-That-Could feels like more than just somewhere to buy bread. Miller + Baker owners Rachel and Mark Taylor. Max Veenhuyzen Restaurant reviews, news and the hottest openings served to your inbox. Sign up Inspired by the sourdough and organic food culture the couple enjoyed while living in Copenhagen, the Taylors returned to Perth and were keen to recreate their experience. One such lesson was the deliciousness and nutritional value of sourdough bread made from good wheat. Fate led the Taylors to the Heggarty family, founders of Natural Intelligence Farming and owners of a wheat farm in Mollerin in the Wheatbelt.



The Heggartys’ regenerative agriculture approach – a system that, in a pesticide-free nutshell, eschews chemical inputs in favour of natural approaches that improve soil health – resonated with what the Taylors were looking for. With wheat (and occasionally rye) supply locked in, they set about learning the finer points of the stone mill they bought from America and began turning this single-origin grain into freshly milled flour: more nutritious and better tasting than commercially sold commodity flours. But hey, don’t take my word for it - take home one of the bakery’s Millers sourdough loaves and taste if for yourself. A hefty rugby ball of a loaf that contains more wholewheat flour than any other core Miller + Baker product, its dense crumb is the colour of milky tea and reveals bold flashes of, well, wheaten richness with each chew. This is not a bread one buys if they need a neutral, flavourless medium. Miller + Baker works with a range of different wheat strains. Miller + Baker It’s also not a big seller. Or at least, according to the Taylors, compared to the bakery’s regular classic sourdough that, due to its reduced wholewheat flour ratio, boasts a crumb with more spring and puffier pockets of air.



You can take away loaves of classic sourdough too, but if you felt like enjoying it in situ, there’s a glass cabinet filled with ace pre-made sandwiches that are dying to meet you. While the sangers are based on combinations that should be familiar to most – roast beef, ham and cheese, chicken and salad – little details in the kitchen ensure what guests are eating is less lunch bar and more café. The chook for the chicken salad number, for instance, is roasted in-house and moistened with a salad dressing packing a healthy jolt of acidity. The result is a flavour that’s closer to an Eastern European potato salad. Served in gaseous baguettes that are more chewy than crisp, the roast beef roll is made with the good stuff that’s been slowly poached on-site until soft and yielding. Kelly Bucksley at Miller + Baker. Miller + Baker



To finish: a sprightly chimichurri sauce that had more to say than most of the lacklustre versions served around town. The top half of the ham and cheese baguette is dabbed at with hot English mustard while the bottom is primed with thick smears of nutty brown butter. Recent sightings of free agent consultant chef Frankie Dawson treading the boards in the Miller + Baker kitchen can only mean good things for the menu. You’ll spy other people of interest in the bakery too. Steven Jackson, a Perth cook that owned St Kilda’s Miss Jackson café, has been managing the kitchen for the past two years while baker Emanuele Vittozzi keeps close watch on the ovens. Between them, they ensure that the pork and fennel sausage roll is chunky in the best possible ways; the croissants are a healthy mix of crisp and that cotton-wool softness; and that the two-pastry pies – shortcrust cases, puff pastry lids – have lift-off. Beyond supporting small producers and quietly raising awareness of good farming and food nutrition, Miller + Baker is building communities in other ways too. The Taylors are partners in cheery Parkside Coffee down the road; they’ve opened another outpost on Hobart Street in North Perth; the cheery staff host a run club; plus the space next to the bakery is now The Mill Room Mercantile, a polished homewares store. It’s amazing what you can achieve by rethinking what a bakery can be. The low-down Atmosphere: the best neighbourhood bakery since sliced (stone-ground, sourdough) bread Go-to dishes: beef and chimichurri baguette, beef and red wine pie, ham and Gruyere croissant Drinks: coffee roasted by Good People Nice Things plus teas, spiced lattes and other cafe favourites Cost: about $40 for two people, excluding drinks and takeaway treats for later Good Food reviews are booked anonymously and paid independently. A restaurant can’t pay for a review or inclusion in the Good Food Guide.

World.title: Netanyahu, Zelensky to meet Trump at White House, attend senator’s funeral
World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaTrump's White House Netanyahu, Zelensky to meet Trump at White House, attend senator’s funeral July 25, 2026 — 2:30am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky are each scheduled to meet with US President Donald Trump next week. Netanyahu will travel to Washington on Monday and will meet with Trump on Tuesday, according to a statement from Netanyahu’s office. Netanyahu will also attend US senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral, his office said. US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House in April 2025. Getty Images The last time Trump and Netanyahu met in Washington was in February, just weeks before they launched a joint war against Iran. Since then, tensions have grown between the longtime allies, including over how to prosecute the war. Israel had opposed Trump’s recent negotiations with Iran, while Trump was upset over Israeli military action in Lebanon, which he saw as a threat to his diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.



Related Article Updated

Middle East at war Trump warns of ‘massive attack’ on Iran, Australians urged to rethink travel plans But with Iran and the United States fighting once again, Israel has also signalled its willingness to rejoin the conflict. In recent days, Israeli officials have said they’re preparing to respond if Iran launches an attack on Israeli soil. Zelensky is also scheduled to meet with Trump on Tuesday, a White House official said. A Ukrainian source said Zelensky was interested in travelling to the United States, but his team was waiting for official confirmation of Trump’s schedule from the White House. The source added that Ukrainians and US officials had been discussing a proposal for an air ceasefire to take to Russian officials, as part of a new round of peace proposals to try to end the war that began in 2022 with Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.



The source said Ukraine had approached Russian President Vladimir Putin in the past with offers of a ceasefire, which had been turned down. However, some officials believe that pressure on Russia’s economy from ongoing Ukrainian drone and missile strikes may soften Putin’s stance. Zelensky spoke on Wednesday with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about the prospects for renewed peace talks with Russia, and said that Ukrainian and US officials could meet in the US in the coming days. Earlier on Friday, right-wing activist and Trump ally Laura Loomer interviewed Zelensky and said he had told her he would likely be in the US next week for a trip that would include a meeting with Trump. Related Article Analysis

US politics Lindsey Graham, the ‘Three Amigos’ and the shifting politics of Israel Loomer, in a post on X, added that Zelensky said he would attend the funeral for Graham, who died earlier this month. A memorial service for the Republican lawmaker will be held on Tuesday in Washington, where Trump will make remarks ahead of a funeral in Graham’s home state of South Carolina on Wednesday.



Graham was a major supporter of Ukraine, travelling there 10 times since the Russian invasion. He pushed for sanctions on Russia as well as US backing for Kyiv. Reuters/AP Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: ‘This is my last decision’: LeBron James heading to 76ers
World.content:
Breaking SportBasketballNBA ‘This is my last decision’: LeBron James heading to 76ers Frank Pingue July 25, 2026 — 2:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

LeBron James announced his decision on Friday (US time) to join the Philadelphia 76ers for his record-extending 24th NBA season with hopes of helping the franchise snap a 43-year championship drought. The league’s all-time leading scorer spent the last eight seasons of his glittering career with the Los Angeles Lakers, leading them to a title in 2020 after two separate stints with the Cleveland Cavaliers and four years with the Miami Heat. Off to Philadelphia: LeBron James. Getty Images “This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship,” James wrote on social media. “I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you, LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always be home!”



James will join a 76ers team that made the 2026 NBA playoffs by securing the seventh seed through a play-in tournament before falling to the eventual champion New York Knicks in the second round. James did not disclose terms of the deal, but ESPN reported that the four-time champion signed a two-year, $US8 million ($11.5 million) contract with a player option. View post on X A number of teams had been pursuing James, with Cleveland, Miami, the Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves all believed to have been interested in the high-profile free agent. The 41-year-old James, who last March surpassed Robert Parish’s record for most career regular-season games played, has continued to perform at an elite level despite his age.



He earned a league-record 22nd consecutive All-Star selection last February during a season in which he averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists over 60 games. His season ended when the Lakers were swept from the second round of the playoffs. Related Article NBA LeBron James is leaving the Lakers. At 41, he plans to play another season “I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn’t ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game. I still truly love this game, and I have more to give,” James said. “The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out.” In a testament to his durability, James and his son Bronny became the first father-son duo to play together in a regular-season NBA game in October 2024, fulfilling what he had long said was one of his remaining basketball goals.



James, a four-time NBA Finals Most Valuable Player, joined the Lakers in 2018. He set the league record for the longest career in NBA history last year when he surpassed Vince Carter’s mark of 22 seasons. Loading He was selected with the first pick in the 2003 NBA Draft by his hometown Cavaliers, where he spent seven seasons before announcing during a live TV special titled The Decision that he was leaving for Miami. The announcement damaged James’ public image and led to many people burning his replica No. 23 jerseys on Cleveland’s streets that night. In Miami, James teamed up with Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh to create an instant powerhouse that won two NBA titles during their four seasons together in South Beach.



Related Article NBA Knicks break their drought and deliver long-awaited sporting glory to New York James returned to Cleveland and in 2016 rallied the team from a 3-1 series deficit in the NBA Finals to stun the Golden State Warriors and make good on his promise to deliver the Cavaliers their first championship. Two years later, James again left his hometown team, where he remains the franchise leader in nearly every major statistical category, to join the Lakers, where for the first time he played in the NBA’s Western Conference.
